🧠 Advanced Trading System — Knowledge Base

chunks.text:
🧠 Advanced Trading System — Knowledge Base > What this covers
What this covers

- Market structure, technicals, fundamentals, derivatives, risk, systems and taxation.
- Indian equities, futures and options with India-specific costs and rules.
- Probabilities, R-multiples and regimes — not tips.
- A tested system before live capital.

**Time commitment:** 8–12 hours/week for 12 weeks (or 4–6 hours/week for 6 months).
Module 13 is a **companion reference** — read it alongside Module 01 and revisit it
after the capstone. Module 14 is the **style-selection lab** — do it before the
capstone or immediately after, so your system fits your time, capital and temperament.

chunks.title: 🧠 Advanced Trading System — Knowledge Base > How to study (the 5-step loop)
chunks.text:
🧠 Advanced Trading System — Knowledge Base > How to study (the 5-step loop)
How to study (the 5-step loop)

1. **Read** the module.
2. **Write** a one-page summary in your own words (Teluglish is fine).
3. **Apply** on 10–20 charts or 3–5 companies.
4. **Backtest** the idea with costs.
5. **Journal** what you learned and what you will change.

> Reading alone creates the illusion of knowledge. Application creates skill.

chunks.title: Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > Learning outcomes
chunks.text:
Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > Learning outcomes
Learning outcomes

By the end, you can:
1. Explain what a share, an index and a derivative are.
2. Trace an order from your app to the depository.
3. Distinguish investing, trading and speculation.
4. Identify the participants on the other side of your trade.
5. Place a simulated trade and compute its costs.

chunks.title: Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 1. What is a share?
chunks.text:
Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 1. What is a share?
1. What is a share?

A share is a unit of **ownership** in a company. If a company has 1 crore shares and
you own 1 lakh, you own 1%. You get:
- a claim on profits (dividends, if declared),
- a vote in certain decisions,
- residual value if the company is wound up (after all creditors).

**Price** is not the company's value; it is the last agreed transaction between a
buyer and a seller. It changes with expectations, flows, news, and liquidity.

**Market capitalisation** = share price × number of shares.
**Enterprise value (EV)** = market cap + debt − cash. EV is closer to what the
business is worth to an acquirer.

---

chunks.title: Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 2. Primary vs secondary market
chunks.text:
Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 2. Primary vs secondary market
2. Primary vs secondary market

| Market | What happens | Who gets money |
|---|---|---|
| **Primary** | Company issues new shares (IPO, FPO, rights, QIP) | Company |
| **Secondary** | Investors trade existing shares on exchange | Seller, not the company |

The exchange is a **secondary market**. IPOs are the primary market. A stock's price
on the exchange does not directly fund the company (except future capital raising).

---

chunks.title: Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 3. What is an index?
chunks.text:
Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 3. What is an index?
3. What is an index?

An index tracks a basket of stocks using a formula (usually free-float market cap).
- **Sensex:** 30 large BSE companies, launched 1986, base 1978-79 = 100.
- **Nifty 50:** 50 large NSE companies, launched 1996, base 3 Nov 1995 = 1000.
- **Bank Nifty:** 12 major banks; high beta.
- Sectoral indices: IT, Pharma, Auto, FMCG, Metal, PSU Bank, Realty.

**Index divisor:** adjusts for corporate actions and constituent changes so the index
is continuous. Index rebalancing creates passive flows — a real trading event.

---

chunks.title: Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 4. Participants
chunks.text:
Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 4. Participants
4. Participants

| Participant | Motivation | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| **Retail** | Wealth, income, excitement | Small size, emotional, heterogeneous |
| **FIIs** | Global allocation | Large, macro-driven, flow-sensitive |
| **DIIs** | Policy/liability matching | Steady, valuation-sensitive |
| **Mutual funds/ETFs** | Track/index/active | Rebalancing flows |
| **Prop desks** | Profit | Fast, risk-managed, often market-neutral |
| **Market makers** | Spread capture | Provide liquidity, hedge Greeks |
| **Arbitrageurs** | Price gaps | Cash-futures, ETF, options |
| **Promoters** | Control/value | Insider info (regulated), long-term |
| **HNIs/family offices** | Wealth | Flexible, concentrated |
| **Algos/HFT** | Microstructure edge | Latency, order flow |

**Key insight:** every trade has a counterparty. Ask why they are willing to take the
other side. If you cannot answer, you may be the liquidity.

---

chunks.title: Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 5. Lifecycle of an order
chunks.text:
Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 5. Lifecycle of an order
5. Lifecycle of an order

```
You (app)
  → Broker (KYC, margin check, risk check)
  → Exchange (order matching engine)
  → Trade confirmation
  → Clearing corporation (novation, margin, settlement guarantee)
  → Depository (NSDL/CDSL: shares)
  → Bank (funds)
```

**T+1:** trade today, settlement tomorrow. Shares/funds move via the clearing system.
**Intraday:** you square off before close; no delivery.

**Order matching:** price-time priority. Best price wins; at the same price, earliest
order wins. Liquidity is not guaranteed — it is other people's orders.

---

chunks.title: Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 6. Investing vs trading vs speculation
chunks.text:
Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 6. Investing vs trading vs speculation
6. Investing vs trading vs speculation

| | Investing | Trading | Speculation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Horizon | Years | Days–months | Minutes–days |
| Edge | Business compounding | Price/flow patterns | Event/volatility |
| Analysis | Fundamentals | Technical + risk | Positioning + catalysts |
| Frequency | Low | Medium | High |
| Cost sensitivity | Low | Medium | Very high |
| Main risk | Business/valuation | Regime/risk | Leverage/tail |

None is morally superior. But **the process, costs and risk limits must match the
horizon**. A long-term investor does not need a 1-minute chart; a scalper cannot use
a 10-year DCF.

---

chunks.title: Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 7. Instrument map
chunks.text:
Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 7. Instrument map
7. Instrument map

| Instrument | What it is | Leverage | Settlement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Equity | Ownership | No (unless intraday) | T+1 |
| ETF | Basket tracking an index/commodity | No | T+1 |
| Futures | Obligation to buy/sell later | Yes (margin) | Cash/MTM daily |
| Options | Right, not obligation | Yes (premium) | Cash (index) / physical (stock) |
| Mutual fund | Pooled portfolio | No | NAV-based |
| REIT/InvIT | Real asset/yield trust | No | T+1 |
| Bonds/G-secs | Lending | No | T+1/T+0 |
| Commodity | Gold, silver, crude, agri | Yes | Cash/delivery |

Start with **equity/ETF cash**; add derivatives only after Module 06 and a backtest.

---

chunks.title: Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 8. Risk and return
chunks.text:
Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 8. Risk and return
8. Risk and return

```
Expected return = risk-free rate + risk premium
```

Higher expected return requires either **more risk** or **more skill/edge**. Leverage
does not create edge; it magnifies outcomes and accelerates ruin.

**Three kinds of risk:**
1. **Market risk** — prices fall (systematic, undiversifiable).
2. **Specific risk** — company/sector problems (diversifiable).
3. **Behavioural risk** — you panic, chase, oversize (the biggest for retail).

---

chunks.title: Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 9. Getting started (India)
chunks.text:
Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 9. Getting started (India)
9. Getting started (India)

1. **PAN + Aadhaar + bank account.**
2. **KYC** with a SEBI-registered broker.
3. **Demat + trading account** (NSDL/CDSL).
4. **Nomination** and contact details.
5. **Funds** via UPI/net banking; understand pay-in/pay-out.
6. **Start with paper trading** or a tiny amount.
7. **Learn order types** before the first market order.
8. **Keep records** from day one (Module 11).

**Broker selection:** regulation, reliability, costs, margin rules, platform stability,
support, API (if algo), and whether you understand the product.

---

chunks.title: Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 10. First trade simulation (do this now, no money)
chunks.text:
Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 10. First trade simulation (do this now, no money)
10. First trade simulation (do this now, no money)

Pick a liquid stock (e.g., a Nifty 50 name). Using a chart and current data:

```
Instrument:
Date/time:
Why this stock:
Trend (daily/weekly):
Entry:
Stop:
Target:
Risk per share:
Quantity for ₹5,000 risk:
Position value:
Estimated costs:
R:R:
Invalidation:
```

Then answer:
- Who might be selling to you, and why?
- What would make you wrong in 24 hours?
- If the stock gaps 3% against you, what is the loss?

---

chunks.title: Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 11. Myths to kill early
chunks.text:
Module 00 — Orientation: How Markets Actually Work > 11. Myths to kill early
11. Myths to kill early

1. "The market is gambling." — No, unmanaged risk is gambling; a process is not.
2. "You need a lot of money." — You need a **positive expectancy** and discipline.
3. "More indicators = better." — More lag, more confusion.
4. "A tip is a shortcut." — A tip without risk is a liability.
5. "Losses are failure." — Losses are the cost of doing business; ruin is failure.
6. "Leverage makes money faster." — It also removes you faster.
7. "Backtest = future." — A backtest is evidence, not a forecast.

---

Module 01 — 150 Years of Indian Markets (1875 → 2026)

chunks.title: Module 01 — 150 Years of Indian Markets (1875 → 2026) > Learning outcomes
chunks.text:
Module 01 — 150 Years of Indian Markets (1875 → 2026) > Learning outcomes
Learning outcomes

1. Explain how BSE and NSE were built and why NSE changed everything.
2. Identify the major scams, crashes and reforms.
3. Extract **trading lessons** from each crisis.
4. Understand why regulation, liquidity and leverage are permanent themes.

---

chunks.title: Module 01 — 150 Years of Indian Markets (1875 → 2026) > 1. The banyan tree era (1850s–1874)
chunks.text:
Module 01 — 150 Years of Indian Markets (1875 → 2026) > 1. The banyan tree era (1850s–1874)
1. The banyan tree era (1850s–1874)

In the 1850s, five brokers — four Gujarati and one Parsi — traded informally under a
banyan tree in front of Bombay's Town Hall. As the group grew, they moved to the
junction of Meadows Street and Esplanade Road.

**Lesson:** markets begin as **trust networks**, not buildings. Liquidity clusters
where traders gather; regulation follows success.

---

chunks.title: Module 01 — 150 Years of Indian Markets (1875 → 2026) > 2. BSE: Asia's oldest exchange (1875)
chunks.text:
Module 01 — 150 Years of Indian Markets (1875 → 2026) > 2. BSE: Asia's oldest exchange (1875)
2. BSE: Asia's oldest exchange (1875)

- **9 July 1875:** Premchand Roychand, the "Cotton King", organised brokers into the
  **Native Share & Stock Brokers' Association**.
- **1899:** permanent headquarters on Dalal Street ("dalal" = broker).
- **1957:** first exchange recognised by the Government of India under the Securities
  Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956.
- **1986:** SENSEX launched (base 1978-79 = 100).
- **1995:** BOLT (BSE On-Line Trading) replaced open-outcry trading.
- **2007:** demutualised and corporatised.
- **2017:** BSE listed on NSE.

**Why it matters:** BSE survived colonial rule, nationalisation, scams and technology
shifts. Longevity came from **adaptation**, not from being right about every cycle.

---

chunks.title: Module 01 — 150 Years of Indian Markets (1875 → 2026) > 3. NSE: the transparency revolution (1992–1994)
chunks.text:
Module 01 — 150 Years of Indian Markets (1875 → 2026) > 3. NSE: the transparency revolution (1992–1994)
3. NSE: the transparency revolution (1992–1994)

After the 1992 scam, India needed a cleaner, electronic market.

- **November 1992:** NSE incorporated on the Pherwani Committee's recommendation.
- **30 June 1994:** wholesale debt market operations began.
- **3 November 1994:** equities segment went live — India's first **screen-based,
  nationwide, anonymous** trading system.
- **1996:** NIFTY 50 launched (base 3 Nov 1995 = 1000).
- **2000:** index futures and options (12 June) — derivatives era.
- **2008:** currency derivatives.
- **2012:** NSE Emerge for SMEs.
- **2017:** NSE IX in GIFT City.
- **2026:** NSE listed on BSE (September 2026).

**Why NSE won:** electronic matching, national access, anonymity, transparency,
standardised margining, and a clean derivative ecosystem. Within a year, its turnover
exceeded BSE's.

**Lesson:** **technology + trust + liquidity** beats incumbency. The same applies to
trading: your edge must adapt to the market's structure.

---

chunks.title: Module 01 — 150 Years of Indian Markets (1875 → 2026) > 4. SEBI: the regulator
chunks.text:
Module 01 — 150 Years of Indian Markets (1875 → 2026) > 4. SEBI: the regulator
4. SEBI: the regulator

- **1988:** SEBI created as an administrative body.
- **1992:** SEBI Act gave it statutory powers after the Harshad Mehta scam.
- Mandate: protect investors, develop the market, regulate intermediaries.
- Key regulations: PFUTP (fraud/manipulation), insider trading, LODR (listing),
  takeover code, broker regulations, research analyst and investment adviser rules.

**Lesson:** regulation is reactive. It follows innovation and fraud. Traders must
track circulars, not just charts.

chunks.title: Module 01 — 150 Years of Indian Markets (1875 → 2026) > 5. Scams and crises — the lesson table
chunks.text:
Module 01 — 150 Years of Indian Markets (1875 → 2026) > 5. Scams and crises — the lesson table
| Year | Event | What happened | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1992** | Harshad Mehta scam | Bank receipts used to divert funds into stocks; ~₹5,000 cr; Sensex manipulated | Leverage + weak settlement = systemic fraud; SEBI Act born |
| **1997** | Asian financial crisis | Currency collapses in Thailand, Korea, Indonesia; contagion | Global flows transmit risk; FIIs can exit fast |
| **2000** | Dotcom bubble | Tech valuations collapsed; global bear market | Narrative ≠ earnings; momentum can reverse violently |
| **2001** | Ketan Parekh scam | Pump-and-dump in tech/media stocks; bank funding | Illiquid stocks + leverage + circular trading = trap |
| **2008** | Global financial crisis | Lehman; credit freeze; Sensex fell >50% | Correlations go to 1 in a crisis; cash is a position |
| **2009** | Satyam fraud | Fake cash/receivables; promoter confession | Cash flow and governance checks matter |
| **2013** | Taper tantrum | Fed taper talk; INR depreciation; outflows | Macro shocks hit emerging markets disproportionately |
| **2016** | Demonetisation | ₹500/₹1000 notes withdrawn; consumption shock | Policy shocks can gap sectors |
| **2018** | PNB/Nirav Modi | ₹13,000+ cr fraud via LoUs | Bank governance and counterparty risk |
| **2020** | COVID crash | Sensex −30% in weeks; then V-shaped rally | Gap risk is real; panic selling often marks lows |
| **2021** | Retail boom | Demat accounts surge; meme/small-cap mania | Flow-driven rallies; valuation discipline ignored |
| **2022** | Rate-hike cycle | Global tightening; tech/growth de-rated | Liquidity drives multiples; discount rates matter |
| **2024–25** | F&O tightening | SEBI raised contract sizes, rationalised weekly expiries, tightened margins | Regulation can kill a strategy overnight |
| **2025** | US tariff shock | "Liberation Day" tariffs; global crash; India–Pakistan conflict | Trade policy + geopolitics = gap risk |
| **2025** | US–India tariff tension | 50% tariff phase; exporters/rupee pressure | Trade dependence is a vulnerability |
| **2026** | Iran war/oil shock | Hormuz disruption; inflation; RBI hawkish turn | War is an inflation shock first |
| **2026** | NSE IPO/listing | NSE listed on BSE (24 Sep 2026) | Market structure is never static |

| Milestone | Approx. period | Meaning |

chunks.text:
Module 01 — 150 Years of Indian Markets (1875 → 2026) > 7. What changed for the retail trader
7. What changed for the retail trader

| Era | Retail reality |
|---|---|
| 1990s | Physical shares, open outcry, broker dependency, no screen |
| 2000s | Online trading, demat, derivatives access |
| 2010s | Discount brokers, mobile apps, ETFs, UPI |
| 2020s | Zero-brokerage delivery, options boom, API/algo, SEBI guardrails |
| 2025–26 | Bigger F&O contracts, expiry rationalisation, algo registration |

**Implication:** access is no longer the edge. **Risk management, data and discipline**
are.

chunks.title: Module 01 — 150 Years of Indian Markets (1875 → 2026) > 8. Seven permanent lessons
chunks.text:
Module 01 — 150 Years of Indian Markets (1875 → 2026) > 8. Seven permanent lessons
8. Seven permanent lessons

1. **Liquidity is a fair-weather friend.** It vanishes when you need it.
2. **Leverage turns a mistake into a funeral.** Position size is survival.
3. **Every bubble has a good story.** Stories don't pay dividends.
4. **Regulation lags fraud.** Verify, don't trust.
5. **Correlations converge in a crisis.** Diversify across factors, not just names.
6. **Cash flow is the truth.** Accounting can be managed; cash is harder.
7. **The market adapts.** An edge that everyone knows is no longer an edge.

| | 1992 scam | 2020 COVID crash |

| Trigger | Fraud + leverage | Exogenous health shock |
| Speed | Slow burn, then collapse | Violent gap down |

Learning outcomes

chunks.title: Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 1. The trading day (IST)
chunks.text:
Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 1. The trading day (IST)
1. The trading day (IST)

| Session | Time | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-open collection | 09:00–09:08 | Orders collected, no matching |
| Pre-open matching | 09:08–09:15 | Equilibrium price discovery |
| Normal market | 09:15–15:30 | Continuous trading |
| Post-close | 15:40–16:00 | Closing price/VWAP trades (verify) |
| Currency | 09:00–17:00 | USDINR etc. |
| Commodity (MCX) | ~09:00–23:30/23:55 | International overlap |

**Why pre-open matters:** overnight news is absorbed in the first 15 minutes. The
opening price can gap far from yesterday's close. Avoid market orders in the first
seconds unless you have a plan.

**Muhurat trading:** a symbolic one-hour Diwali session; liquidity is thin.

---

chunks.title: Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 2. Order types — when to use what
chunks.text:
Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 2. Order types — when to use what
2. Order types — when to use what

| Order | Execution | Best use | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Market** | Best available price | Liquid stocks, urgent exit | Slippage |
| **Limit** | Your price or better | Controlled entry/exit | No fill |
| **SL (stop-loss limit)** | Trigger → limit order | Price-controlled stop | Gap/no fill |
| **SL-M** | Trigger → market order | Certain exit | Price uncertainty |
| **IOC** | Immediate or cancel | Slicing, arbitrage | Partial/no fill |
| **GTT** | Good-till-triggered | Swing stop/target | Broker-specific |
| **AMO** | After-market order | Next-day entry | Price gap |
| **Iceberg** | Sliced large order | Reduce impact | Complexity |
| **Bracket/Cover** | Entry + SL + target | Intraday managed trade | Broker rules |

**Practical rules:**
- Liquid large caps: limit order with 0.1–0.2% buffer.
- Illiquid stocks/options: never market order; work the limit.
- Stops: SL-M for certainty; SL for price control. Accept that neither guarantees a fill.
- Avoid placing stops exactly at round numbers; use structure + ATR buffer.

---

chunks.title: Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 3. Product types
chunks.text:
Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 3. Product types
3. Product types

| Product | Meaning | Settlement | Leverage |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CNC** | Cash & carry, delivery | T+1 | No (full payment) |
| **MIS** | Intraday, square off same day | Same day | Broker leverage |
| **NRML** | Normal carry-forward derivatives | Daily MTM | Margin-based |

**Intraday leverage** is broker-specific and regulated. It is not free money; it
amplifies both gains and losses and can trigger forced square-off.

---

chunks.title: Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 4. Settlement
chunks.text:
Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 4. Settlement
4. Settlement

**Equity:** T+1. Buy today → shares credited tomorrow. Sell today → funds per broker
pay-out cycle. T+0 optional is expanding in phases.

**Derivatives:** futures and index options are cash-settled; stock options are
physically settled. If a short stock option expires ITM, you may be assigned and
must deliver shares.

**Pay-in/pay-out:** ensure funds/shares are available. A failed pay-in can lead to
auction, penalties and a broker default risk.

---

chunks.title: Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 5. Margins
chunks.text:
Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 5. Margins
5. Margins

| Margin | What it is |
|---|---|
| **SPAN** | Portfolio risk margin (worst-case scenarios) |
| **Exposure** | Additional buffer, typically 3%+ |
| **ELM** | Extreme loss margin for options |
| **Peak margin** | Upfront collection; no free intraday leverage |
| **Intraday monitoring** | SEBI requires monitoring during the day |

**Hedged positions** (spreads, condors) get lower margin. But margin benefit rules
change; verify on the broker's calculator.

**Margin call:** if MTM loss reduces free margin, the broker may square off. Keep
30–50% free margin.

---

chunks.title: Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 6. Circuit limits and halts
chunks.text:
Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 6. Circuit limits and halts
6. Circuit limits and halts

**Stock bands:** 2%, 5%, 10%, 20% depending on the stock. F&O stocks have dynamic
bands. When the band is hit, trading may halt or move to auction.

**Index circuit breakers:**

| Trigger | Before 13:00 | 13:00–14:30 | After 14:30 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10% | 45-min halt | 15-min halt | No halt |
| 15% | 1h 45m halt | 45-min halt | No halt |
| 20% | Rest of day | Rest of day | Rest of day |

**Implication:** a stop-loss is not a guarantee. Size positions so a gap through the
stop is survivable.

---

chunks.title: Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 7. The true cost of a trade > Equity delivery example (₹1,00,000 buy + sell)
chunks.text:
Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 7. The true cost of a trade > Equity delivery example (₹1,00,000 buy + sell)
Equity delivery example (₹1,00,000 buy + sell)
Assume discount broker, 0 brokerage.

| Cost | Buy | Sell |
|---|---|---|
| STT 0.1% | ₹100 | ₹100 |
| Exchange 0.00325% | ₹3.25 | ₹3.25 |
| SEBI ₹10/cr | ₹0.10 | ₹0.10 |
| GST 18% on (brokerage+exchange) | ₹0.59 | ₹0.59 |
| Stamp 0.015% | ₹15 | — |
| DP charge | — | ₹15–30 |
| **Total** | **~₹119** | **~₹149** |

Round trip ≈ **₹268 = 0.27%** before slippage. A 0.5% target is mostly costs.

chunks.title: Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 7. The true cost of a trade > Futures example (1 lot, ₹18.75 lakh notional)
chunks.text:
Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 7. The true cost of a trade > Futures example (1 lot, ₹18.75 lakh notional)
Futures example (1 lot, ₹18.75 lakh notional)
- STT 0.02% on sell ≈ ₹375
- Exchange ~0.0019% ≈ ₹35
- GST/brokerage/sebi/stamp ≈ ₹60–100
- **Total ≈ ₹500–550 per round trip** + slippage.

chunks.title: Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 7. The true cost of a trade > Options example (premium ₹1,20,000 sell)
chunks.text:
Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 7. The true cost of a trade > Options example (premium ₹1,20,000 sell)
Options example (premium ₹1,20,000 sell)
- STT 0.1% on sell premium = ₹120
- Exchange ~0.035% = ₹42
- Brokerage/GST/stamp ≈ ₹30–50
- **Total ≈ ₹200+** per round trip, plus bid-ask spread.

**Rule:** if the expected gross edge is < 2× round-trip cost, skip the trade.

chunks.title: Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 8. Liquidity and impact cost
chunks.text:
Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 8. Liquidity and impact cost
8. Liquidity and impact cost

**Bid-ask spread** = best ask − best bid. **Impact cost** = price move caused by your
own order.

| Liquidity | Spread | Impact | Strategy |
|---|---|---|---|
| High (large cap, index) | Tight | Low | Market/limit fine |
| Medium (midcap) | Moderate | Medium | Limit, slice |
| Low (smallcap, far OTM) | Wide | High | Avoid or tiny size |

**Check before trading:** average daily volume, delivery percentage, market depth,
circuit history, operator/pump risk.

**VWAP** = traded value / traded volume. Institutional benchmark; useful for
execution quality.

---

chunks.title: Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 9. Corporate actions
chunks.text:
Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 9. Corporate actions
9. Corporate actions

| Action | Effect | Adjustment |
|---|---|---|
| Dividend | Cash to holder | Price drops on ex-date |
| Bonus | Free shares | Price adjusts proportionally |
| Split | More shares, lower price | Adjust history |
| Rights | Discounted shares | Adjust for rights value |
| Buyback | Company buys shares | Tender/auction |
| Merger/demerger | Scheme | Price/share adjustment |

**Backtests must use adjusted prices.** Otherwise splits/bonuses create fake crashes.

chunks.title: Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 10. IPOs and primary market
chunks.text:
Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 10. IPOs and primary market
10. IPOs and primary market

- **IPO:** apply via UPI/ASBA; money blocked, not debited.
- **Lot size/price band:** in the RHP.
- **Allotment:** lottery for oversubscribed retail.
- **Listing gain:** not guaranteed; GMP is sentiment, not valuation.
- **OFS:** existing holders sell; no fresh capital.
- **SME IPOs:** high risk, low liquidity.

**IPO checklist:** business, promoter, financials, valuation vs peers, use of proceeds,
lock-in, anchor investors, market regime.

---

chunks.title: Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 11. F&O ban list
chunks.text:
Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 11. F&O ban list
11. F&O ban list

When open interest in a stock future crosses **95% of the market-wide position limit**,
the exchange puts it in the ban list. Only reducing positions are allowed until OI
falls below 80%. This can trap you in a position.

**Check the ban list daily** if you trade stock F&O.

---

chunks.title: Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 12. Worked example — full trade
chunks.text:
Module 02 — Market Mechanics: Sessions, Orders, Settlement, Costs > 12. Worked example — full trade
12. Worked example — full trade

```
Capital: ₹5,00,000
Stock: ABC (liquid large cap)
Entry: ₹500
Stop: ₹485 (3 ATR-ish)
Risk/unit: ₹15
Risk budget: 1% = ₹5,000
Quantity: 333 → round to 300 (lot-free equity)
Position: ₹1,50,000 (30% of capital)
Target: ₹545 (3R)
Costs: ~0.27% round trip ≈ ₹405
Slippage: 0.1% each side ≈ ₹300
Net R:R after costs: (45×300 − 705) / (15×300 + 705) = 12,795/5,205 ≈ 2.46:1
```

**Check:** position 30% is high for a single trade; consider 15–20% cap or a smaller
risk budget. The point is to **see the true numbers** before entering.

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 1. Dow Theory — the foundation
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 1. Dow Theory — the foundation
1. Dow Theory — the foundation

1. **Averages discount everything** — price reflects known information.
2. **Three trends** — primary (months/years), secondary (weeks/months), minor (days).
3. **Primary trends have three phases** — accumulation, public participation, distribution.
4. **Averages must confirm each other** — index/sector breadth.
5. **Volume must confirm the trend** — expansion in the trend direction.
6. **A trend persists until a clear reversal** — don't anticipate, confirm.

**Modern use:** trend + breadth + volume. Ignore the archaic parts; keep the logic.

---

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 2. Market structure
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 2. Market structure
2. Market structure

```
Uptrend:    HH + HL
Downtrend:  LH + LL
Range:      equal highs/lows, repeated rejection
```

**Break of structure (BOS):** close beyond the last swing in trend direction.
**Change of character (CHoCH):** break of the last opposing swing → possible reversal.

**Mechanical swing rule:** a swing high is a bar with 2 lower highs on each side; a
swing low is a bar with 2 higher lows on each side. Use consistently.

**Timeframe alignment:** trade in the direction of the weekly/daily; use 15m/5m only
for timing.

---

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 3. Support and resistance
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 3. Support and resistance
3. Support and resistance

- Zones, not lines: use the cluster of wicks/bodies.
- **Role reversal:** broken resistance becomes support.
- **Freshness:** first/second retest is stronger; 4th+ test is weak.
- **Confluence:** prior structure + trendline + Fibonacci + round number + VWAP.
- **Liquidity:** equal highs/lows attract stop runs; expect sweeps.

**How to draw:** start from the most recent major swing, mark the obvious reaction
levels, then refine with the higher timeframe. Fewer levels = better.

---

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 4. Candlesticks — context first
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 4. Candlesticks — context first
4. Candlesticks — context first

| Pattern | Signal | Confirmation |
|---|---|---|
| Hammer/pin bar | Rejection of lows | Volume + at support |
| Shooting star | Rejection of highs | Volume + at resistance |
| Bullish/bearish engulfing | Momentum shift | Close beyond prior body |
| Inside bar | Compression | Break of mother bar |
| Outside bar | Expansion | Close direction |
| Doji | Indecision | Wait |
| Morning/evening star | 3-bar reversal | Volume + level |
| Marubozu | Conviction | Not at exhaustion |
| Three soldiers/crows | Continuation | Volume |
| Harami | Slowdown | Confirmation |
| Tweezer | Double rejection | Level |

**Formula:** body = |C−O|; range = H−L; upper wick = H−max(O,C); lower wick =
min(O,C)−L. Pin bar: wick ≥ 2× body, close in top/bottom third.

**Warning:** standalone candlestick win rates are weak. Use them as **timing triggers**
inside structure.

---

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 5. Chart patterns > Reversal
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 5. Chart patterns > Reversal
Reversal
- Head & shoulders: 3 peaks, neckline break; target = head − neckline.
- Double/triple top/bottom: equal extremes; target = height.
- Rounding bottom: slow accumulation; target = depth.
- Wedge: converging; breakout often retests.

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 5. Chart patterns > Continuation
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 5. Chart patterns > Continuation
Continuation
- Flag/pennant: flagpole measured move.
- Triangle (ascending/descending/symmetrical): height at breakout.
- Cup & handle: cup depth target.
- Rectangle: range height.

**Rules:**
1. Volume contracts in consolidation, expands on breakout.
2. Breakout needs a **close** beyond the boundary.
3. Retest improves probability, lowers R:R.
4. Most patterns fail in ranges; trade with regime.
5. Measure from breakout, not pattern start.

---

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 6. Moving averages
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 6. Moving averages
6. Moving averages

```
SMA(n) = average of last n closes
EMA(n) = close×k + EMA_prev×(1−k), k=2/(n+1)
```

| MA | Use |
|---|---|
| 20 EMA | Short-term dynamic support |
| 50 EMA | Swing trend |
| 100/200 EMA | Primary trend |
| 50/200 cross | Golden/death cross (slow regime signal) |

**Rules:** price above rising MA = bullish; MA slope matters more than the cross.
MAs lag; don't use them as standalone entry triggers.

---

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 7. RSI, MACD, ATR, Bollinger, ADX > RSI (14)
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 7. RSI, MACD, ATR, Bollinger, ADX > RSI (14)
RSI (14)
```
RSI = 100 − 100/(1+RS), RS = avg gain/avg loss
```
- 40–60 = neutral; >70 overbought; <30 oversold.
- In trends, overbought can persist. Use divergence + structure.
- Failure swings are more reliable than raw levels.

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 7. RSI, MACD, ATR, Bollinger, ADX > MACD
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 7. RSI, MACD, ATR, Bollinger, ADX > MACD
MACD
```
MACD = EMA12 − EMA26; Signal = EMA9(MACD); Hist = MACD − Signal
```
- Crossovers, zero-line, divergence.
- Whipsaws in ranges; combine with trend filter.

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 7. RSI, MACD, ATR, Bollinger, ADX > ATR (14)
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 7. RSI, MACD, ATR, Bollinger, ADX > ATR (14)
ATR (14)
```
TR = max(H−L, |H−prevC|, |L−prevC|)
ATR = average TR
```
- Stop = 1.5–3 ATR beyond structure.
- ATR% = ATR/price for cross-stock comparison.
- Position size = risk ₹ / (k×ATR).

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 7. RSI, MACD, ATR, Bollinger, ADX > Bollinger Bands
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 7. RSI, MACD, ATR, Bollinger, ADX > Bollinger Bands
Bollinger Bands
```
Mid = SMA20; Upper/Lower = Mid ± 2×σ20
Bandwidth = (Upper−Lower)/Mid
```
- Squeeze = volatility contraction → expansion.
- Walking the band = trend; don't fade blindly.

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 7. RSI, MACD, ATR, Bollinger, ADX > ADX (14)
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 7. RSI, MACD, ATR, Bollinger, ADX > ADX (14)
ADX (14)
- >25 trending; <20 range.
- +DI/−DI direction; ADX strength.
- Use to choose strategy (trend vs mean reversion).

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 8. Volume
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 8. Volume
8. Volume

| Price | Volume | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Up | Up | Healthy demand |
| Up | Down | Weak rally |
| Down | Up | Distribution/panic |
| Down | Down | Dry-up |
| Breakout | High | Conviction (climax risk) |
| Pullback | Low | Healthy |

**VSA:** no demand, no supply, stopping volume, climax, test.
**OBV:** cumulative signed volume; divergence is a warning.
**VWAP:** institutional benchmark; anchored VWAP from events.

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 9. Multi-timeframe workflow
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 9. Multi-timeframe workflow
9. Multi-timeframe workflow

```
1. Weekly: trend, major S/R, regime.
2. Daily: structure, pattern, volume, indicator.
3. 60m/15m: entry zone, confluence.
4. 5m: trigger only.
```

**Alignment rule:** if weekly and daily disagree, reduce size or wait. Counter-trend
trades need a confirmed CHoCH + volume + retest.

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 10. Entry models > Trend pullback
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 10. Entry models > Trend pullback
Trend pullback
- Trend up; pullback to 20/50 EMA or 0.382–0.618 Fib.
- Rejection candle + volume dry-up.
- Entry above candle high; stop below swing; target prior high/extension.

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 10. Entry models > Breakout
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 10. Entry models > Breakout
Breakout
- Squeeze/consolidation; close beyond range on volume >1.5× avg.
- Entry breakout or retest; stop below range; target measured move.

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 10. Entry models > Mean reversion
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 10. Entry models > Mean reversion
Mean reversion
- Range regime; price at band/S/R; rejection + divergence.
- Stop beyond extreme; target mid-range/VWAP.

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 10. Entry models > Failed breakout
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 10. Entry models > Failed breakout
Failed breakout
- Break then close back inside; volume spike + rejection.
- Entry reversal; stop beyond sweep; target opposite side.

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 11. A complete example
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 11. A complete example
11. A complete example

```
Instrument: NIFTY 50 (daily)
Regime: uptrend (price > rising 50/200 EMA, ADX 28)
Structure: HH/HL; last swing low 24,600
Pullback: to 20 EMA at 24,850; volume dry-up
Trigger: bullish engulfing close 24,920
Entry: 24,930
Stop: 24,600 (below swing; 1.3% risk)
Target 1: 25,400 (prior high)
Target 2: 25,700 (extension)
Risk: 330 points; reward T1: 470 → 1.42R; T2: 770 → 2.33R
Size: capital ₹5L, 1% = ₹5,000; lot 75 (verify) → risk/lot ₹24,750 > budget
→ use options spread or skip futures; this is the lot-size reality check.
```

**Lesson:** the setup can be right but the instrument too big. Use options spreads,
smaller Underlyings, or skip.

chunks.title: Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 12. Common mistakes
chunks.text:
Module 03 — Technical Analysis: Structure, Patterns, Indicators > 12. Common mistakes
12. Common mistakes

1. Indicator soup (8 lagging signals).
2. Trendlines drawn to fit bias.
3. Buying resistance because "it looks strong".
4. Ignoring volume on breakouts.
5. Stops at obvious levels without buffer.
6. Using 1m charts with 1% risk and high costs.
7. Treating a pattern as a system.
8. No invalidation.
9. Optimising parameters on one stock.
10. Forgetting gaps/circuits override technical levels.

Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile

chunks.title: Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > Learning outcomes
chunks.text:
Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > Learning outcomes
Learning outcomes

1. Identify Wyckoff accumulation/distribution phases and springs/upthrusts.
2. Use Elliott Wave for scenario planning, not prediction.
3. Apply SMC/ICT concepts with mechanical rules and realistic expectations.

chunks.title: Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 1. Wyckoff method > Three laws
chunks.text:
Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 1. Wyckoff method > Three laws
Three laws
1. **Supply and demand** — imbalance moves price.
2. **Cause and effect** — accumulation/distribution builds the cause; markup/markdown is the effect.
3. **Effort vs result** — volume (effort) should produce price movement (result); divergence = absorption.

chunks.title: Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 1. Wyckoff method > Accumulation schematic
chunks.text:
Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 1. Wyckoff method > Accumulation schematic
Accumulation schematic
```
PS (preliminary support)
→ SC (selling climax)
→ AR (automatic rally)
→ ST (secondary test)
→ Spring / Test
→ LPS (last point of support)
→ SOS (sign of strength)
→ Markup
```

chunks.title: Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 1. Wyckoff method > Distribution schematic
chunks.text:
Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 1. Wyckoff method > Distribution schematic
Distribution schematic
```
PSY (preliminary supply)
→ BC (buying climax)
→ AR (automatic reaction)
→ ST (secondary test)
→ UT / UTAD (upthrust after distribution)
→ LPSY (last point of supply)
→ SOW (sign of weakness)
→ Markdown
```

chunks.title: Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 1. Wyckoff method > Mechanical rules (example)
chunks.text:
Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 1. Wyckoff method > Mechanical rules (example)
Mechanical rules (example)
- **Spring:** price breaks below support, closes back above within 3 bars, volume > 1.5× average, followed by SOS.
- **UTAD:** price breaks above resistance, closes back below within 3 bars, volume spike, followed by SOW.
- **Entry:** on LPS retest after SOS; stop below spring/UTAD extreme.
- **Invalidation:** price closes beyond the extreme and holds.

chunks.title: Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 1. Wyckoff method > Wyckoff checklist
chunks.text:
Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 1. Wyckoff method > Wyckoff checklist
Wyckoff checklist
```
[ ] Trading range defined (support/resistance)
[ ] Volume behaviour at extremes
[ ] Spring/upthrust identified
[ ] SOS/SOW confirmation
[ ] LPS/LPSY retest
[ ] Cause size (range width/time) vs effect target
[ ] Higher-timeframe trend alignment
```

chunks.title: Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 2. Elliott Wave > Structure
chunks.text:
Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 2. Elliott Wave > Structure
Structure
- **Impulse:** 5 waves (1-2-3-4-5) in trend direction.
- **Correction:** 3 waves (A-B-C) against trend.

chunks.title: Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 2. Elliott Wave > Three unbreakable rules
chunks.text:
Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 2. Elliott Wave > Three unbreakable rules
Three unbreakable rules
1. Wave 2 never retraces >100% of wave 1.
2. Wave 3 is never the shortest of 1, 3, 5.
3. Wave 4 never enters wave 1 territory (non-diagonal impulse).

chunks.title: Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 2. Elliott Wave > Guidelines
chunks.text:
Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 2. Elliott Wave > Guidelines
Guidelines
- Alternation (wave 2 simple, wave 4 complex).
- Channeling.
- Fibonacci: 0.382, 0.5, 0.618 retracements; 1.618 extensions.
- Wave 3 often extends.

chunks.title: Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 2. Elliott Wave > Honest use
chunks.text:
Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 2. Elliott Wave > Honest use
Honest use
- Multiple counts are valid. Use Elliott to **define scenarios and invalidation**,
  not to predict a precise top/bottom.
- If the count changes daily, it is storytelling, not analysis.
- Combine with volume, structure and market breadth.

chunks.title: Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 3. SMC / ICT concepts
chunks.text:
Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 3. SMC / ICT concepts
3. SMC / ICT concepts

| Concept | Definition | Practical rule |
|---|---|---|
| **Liquidity sweep** | Stop run above/below equal highs/lows | Wait for rejection + CHoCH |
| **Order block** | Last opposing candle before displacement | Entry on retest, stop beyond block |
| **Fair value gap (FVG)** | Imbalance between candles | Price often revisits 50% of gap |
| **BOS** | Break of structure in trend | Continuation entry on retest |
| **CHoCH** | Break of last opposing swing | Reversal signal, confirm volume |
| **Premium/discount** | Above/below 50% of range | Buy discount, sell premium in range |
| **Killzone** | High-liquidity windows | 09:15–11:00, 13:30–15:00 IST |
| **Judas swing** | False move at open | Fade after sweep |
| **Power of 3** | Accumulation–manipulation–distribution | Intraday template |

chunks.title: Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 3. SMC / ICT concepts > Mechanical SMC setup (example)
chunks.text:
Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 3. SMC / ICT concepts > Mechanical SMC setup (example)
Mechanical SMC setup (example)
1. Daily bias: bullish (HH/HL).
2. London/NY or India open sweep of Asian low.
3. CHoCH on 5m with displacement.
4. Entry at 50% of order block/FVG.
5. Stop below sweep low.
6. Target prior high/liquidity pool.
7. Invalidation: close below sweep low.

chunks.title: Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 3. SMC / ICT concepts > Reality check
chunks.text:
Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 3. SMC / ICT concepts > Reality check
Reality check
- Order blocks/FVGs are zones, not magic.
- Most SMC claims are untested; backtest exact rules.
- Without higher-timeframe bias and risk control, SMC is just another pattern.

---

chunks.title: Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 4. VSA — volume spread analysis
chunks.text:
Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 4. VSA — volume spread analysis
4. VSA — volume spread analysis

| Signal | Anatomy | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| No demand | Up bar, narrow spread, low volume | Weakness |
| No supply | Down bar, narrow spread, low volume | Strength |
| Stopping volume | High volume, wide spread, close off lows | Absorption |
| Climax | Extreme volume, wide spread | Exhaustion |
| Test | Low-volume probe of supply | Confirmation |
| Upthrust | High-volume breakout that fails | Distribution |
| Shakeout | High-volume break of support that recovers | Accumulation |

**Rule:** compare volume to the **average of the last 20–30 bars**, and read the
**close location** within the range. A high-volume bar that closes mid-range is
absorption, not conviction.

---

chunks.title: Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 5. Market profile / auction theory
chunks.text:
Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 5. Market profile / auction theory
5. Market profile / auction theory

- **TPO:** time spent at each price.
- **Value area (VA):** 70% of TPOs; VAH/VAL.
- **POC:** most-traded price = fair value.
- **Initial balance (IB):** first hour range.
- **Day types:** trend, normal, normal variation, neutral, double distribution.

**Uses:**
- Acceptance above VAH = bullish; rejection = fade.
- Single prints = imbalance; often revisited.
- Open outside value + acceptance = trend day.
- Open inside value + rotation = range day.

**Best on:** index futures, liquid large caps.

---

chunks.title: Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 6. Order flow and tape reading
chunks.text:
Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 6. Order flow and tape reading
6. Order flow and tape reading

| Concept | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Bid/ask spread** | Liquidity cost |
| **Market depth** | Visible resting orders |
| **Footprint** | Volume at bid/ask per price |
| **Delta** | Aggressive buyers − sellers |
| **Absorption** | Large passive order absorbs aggression |
| **Iceberg** | Hidden size |
| **Spoofing** | Fake orders (illegal) |

**Retail reality:** true order-flow data is limited/expensive in India. Use market
depth, volume, and VWAP as proxies. Do not over-interpret Level 2.

---

chunks.title: Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 7. Intermarket and macro context
chunks.text:
Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 7. Intermarket and macro context
7. Intermarket and macro context

- **Dollar index (DXY)** inverse for EM equities/commodities.
- **US 10-year yield** up → pressure on high-P/E growth.
- **Crude** up → India CAD/inflation pressure; negative for importers.
- **Gold** → risk-off/real yields.
- **India VIX** → option pricing/fear.
- **FII/DII flows** → short-term demand.
- **USDINR** → IT/pharma exporters vs importers.

**Rule:** macro sets the **regime**, technicals set the **timing**, risk sets the **size**.

---

chunks.title: Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 8. Combining frameworks — confluence playbook
chunks.text:
Module 04 — Advanced Price Action: Wyckoff, Elliott, SMC, VSA, Market Profile > 8. Combining frameworks — confluence playbook
8. Combining frameworks — confluence playbook

```
1. Macro/regime: trend, volatility, event calendar.
2. Weekly/daily: structure, Wyckoff phase, key levels.
3. Intraday: market profile day type, VWAP, liquidity.
4. Setup: pullback/breakout/failed breakout + VSA confirmation.
5. Entry: order block/FVG/retest with tight invalidation.
6. Risk: 0.5–1%, stop beyond structure, target liquidity pool.
7. Management: partial at 1R, trail at structure, time stop.
```

**Confluence score (0–6):** trend, structure, volume, level, regime, catalyst.
Trade only ≥4; size up only at 5–6 (within risk limits).

---

chunks.text:

P&L
Revenue → COGS → gross profit → opex → EBITDA → D&A → EBIT → interest → tax → PAT.

chunks.title: Module 05 — Fundamental Analysis: Quality, Valuation, Forensics > 1. The three statements > Balance sheet
chunks.text:
Module 05 — Fundamental Analysis: Quality, Valuation, Forensics > 1. The three statements > Balance sheet
Balance sheet
Assets = Liabilities + Equity.
- Current: cash, receivables, inventory.
- Non-current: PP&E, intangibles, goodwill, CWIP.
- Liabilities: payables, debt, provisions.
- Equity: share capital, reserves.

Watch: goodwill, capitalised expenses, CWIP, contingent liabilities, off-balance-sheet.

chunks.title: Module 05 — Fundamental Analysis: Quality, Valuation, Forensics > 1. The three statements > Cash flow
chunks.text:
Module 05 — Fundamental Analysis: Quality, Valuation, Forensics > 1. The three statements > Cash flow
Cash flow
- **CFO** — operations (truth test).
- **CFI** — capex/acquisitions.
- **CFF** — debt/equity/dividends.
- **FCF = CFO − capex.**

**Quality test:** CFO should track or exceed PAT over a cycle.

chunks.title: Module 05 — Fundamental Analysis: Quality, Valuation, Forensics > 2. Ratio toolkit > Growth
chunks.text:
Module 05 — Fundamental Analysis: Quality, Valuation, Forensics > 2. Ratio toolkit > Growth
Growth
```
CAGR = (End/Start)^(1/n) − 1
Revenue, EBITDA, PAT, EPS, FCF CAGR
Volume vs price growth
```

chunks.title: Module 05 — Fundamental Analysis: Quality, Valuation, Forensics > 2. Ratio toolkit > Profitability
chunks.text:
Module 05 — Fundamental Analysis: Quality, Valuation, Forensics > 2. Ratio toolkit > Profitability
Profitability
```
Gross margin = (Revenue − COGS)/Revenue
EBITDA margin = EBITDA/Revenue
Net margin = PAT/Revenue
ROE = PAT/Average equity
ROCE = EBIT/(Total assets − Current liabilities)
ROIC = NOPAT/Invested capital
DuPont: ROE = Net margin × Asset turnover × Equity multiplier
```

chunks.title: Module 05 — Fundamental Analysis: Quality, Valuation, Forensics > 4. Valuation > DCF (FCFF)
chunks.text:
Module 05 — Fundamental Analysis: Quality, Valuation, Forensics > 4. Valuation > DCF (FCFF)
DCF (FCFF)
```
FCFF = EBIT(1−tax) + D&A − Capex − ΔWC
WACC = (E/V)Ke + (D/V)Kd(1−tax)
TV = FCFF_terminal/(WACC − g)
EV = Σ FCFF/(1+WACC)^t + TV/(1+WACC)^n
Equity = EV − Net debt − Minority + Investments
```
**Ke (CAPM)** = Rf + β×ERP. Indian Rf ~ G-sec; ERP 5–7%; add size/illiquidity/governance.

**Sensitivity:** WACC ±1%, g ±0.5%, margin ±100bps. Show a range, not a point.

chunks.title: Module 05 — Fundamental Analysis: Quality, Valuation, Forensics > 7. Forensic red flags (India)
chunks.text:
Module 05 — Fundamental Analysis: Quality, Valuation, Forensics > 7. Forensic red flags (India)
7. Forensic red flags (India)

1. Cash doesn't earn interest income.
2. Receivables grow faster than sales.
3. Inventory grows faster than sales.
4. CFO persistently below PAT.
5. CWIP stuck for years.
6. High goodwill after acquisitions.
7. Frequent subsidiary restructuring.
8. Loans to related parties.
9. Promoter pledge >30–40%.
10. Auditor resignation/qualification.
11. Tax rate far below statutory.
12. Other income > operating profit.
13. Frequent dilution/preferential allotment.
14. Sudden margin expansion without explanation.
15. Receivable days >120 in a "cash business".
16. Contingent liabilities in notes.
17. Split/bonus + social media hype.
18. Round-tripping with related parties.

**Workflow:** auditor report → notes → related-party schedule → cash flow → working
capital → peers → exchange filings (pledge, ratings, defaults).

chunks.title: Module 06 — Derivatives & Options: Pricing, Greeks, Strategies > 1. Futures
chunks.text:
Module 06 — Derivatives & Options: Pricing, Greeks, Strategies > 1. Futures
1. Futures

```
F = S × e^((r−q)T)
Basis = F − S
Fair value ≈ S + carry − dividends
```

- **Contango:** F > S (carry cost).
- **Backwardation:** F < S (convenience yield/hedging pressure).
- **Roll yield:** return from rolling to the next contract.
- **MTM:** daily cash settlement; a correct view can be stopped by margin calls.

**Uses:** leverage, hedging, arbitrage, pair trades.
**Risks:** leverage, gap, liquidity, roll cost, margin spike, basis risk.

---

chunks.title: Module 06 — Derivatives & Options: Pricing, Greeks, Strategies > 2. Options basics
chunks.text:
Module 06 — Derivatives & Options: Pricing, Greeks, Strategies > 2. Options basics
2. Options basics

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Call/Put | Right to buy/sell |
| Premium | Price of the option |
| Strike (K) | Exercise price |
| Spot (S) | Underlying price |
| ITM/ATM/OTM | Moneyness |
| Intrinsic | Call max(S−K,0); Put max(K−S,0) |
| Time value | Premium − intrinsic |
| European | Exercise at expiry (index) |
| American | Exercise anytime (stock) |
| Cash settled | Index options |
| Physical settled | Stock options |

**Long option:** limited loss (premium), negative theta.
**Short option:** limited gain, large risk, positive theta, margin.

chunks.title: Module 06 — Derivatives & Options: Pricing, Greeks, Strategies > 3. Black-Scholes and parity
chunks.text:
Module 06 — Derivatives & Options: Pricing, Greeks, Strategies > 3. Black-Scholes and parity
3. Black-Scholes and parity

```
C = S·N(d1) − K·e^(−rT)·N(d2)
P = K·e^(−rT)·N(−d2) − S·N(−d1)
d1 = [ln(S/K) + (r + σ²/2)T]/(σ√T)
d2 = d1 − σ√T
```

**Assumptions:** lognormal returns, constant vol, no jumps, continuous trading, no
costs, known dividends, constant rates. Real markets violate all of them — hence skew
and fat tails.

**Put-call parity:**
```
C − P = S − K·e^(−rT)
```
Violations = arbitrage after costs/dividends/borrow.

---

chunks.title: Module 06 — Derivatives & Options: Pricing, Greeks, Strategies > 4. Greeks
chunks.text:
Module 06 — Derivatives & Options: Pricing, Greeks, Strategies > 4. Greeks
4. Greeks

| Greek | Long call | Long put | Short call | Short put | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delta | + | − | − | + | Price sensitivity |
| Gamma | + | + | − | − | Delta instability |
| Theta | − | − | + | + | Time decay |
| Vega | + | + | − | − | IV sensitivity |
| Rho | + | − | − | + | Rate sensitivity |

**Portfolio Greeks:** sum delta-weighted. Delta-neutral ≠ risk-free (gamma, theta, vega).

**Dollar delta** = delta × multiplier × spot.

**Gamma scalping:** long gamma + delta hedge profits if realised vol > implied vol.

**Theta:** ATM loses fastest in the last 2–3 weeks. Weekly options are expensive
lottery tickets unless timed with a catalyst.

---

chunks.title: Module 06 — Derivatives & Options: Pricing, Greeks, Strategies > 5. Implied volatility
chunks.text:
Module 06 — Derivatives & Options: Pricing, Greeks, Strategies > 5. Implied volatility
5. Implied volatility

- **IV** = market's implied future volatility.
- **HV** = realised historical volatility.
- **IV > HV:** options expensive → sellers have an edge (if IV mean-reverts).
- **IV < HV:** options cheap → buyers have an edge.
- **IV rank/percentile:** current IV vs past year.
- **Term structure:** near vs far; event humps.
- **Skew:** OTM puts usually richer.
- **IV crush:** post-event collapse; long premium loses even if direction is right.

**Rule:** trade the spread between implied and expected realised volatility, not just
direction.

---

chunks.text:

Debit / directional

| Strategy | View | Legs | Max profit | Max loss | Breakeven |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Long call | Bullish | Buy call | Unlimited | Premium | K + premium |
| Long put | Bearish | Buy put | K − premium | Premium | K − premium |
| Bull call spread | Mild bullish | Buy low K call, sell high K call | Width − debit | Debit | Low K + debit |
| Bear put spread | Mild bearish | Buy high K put, sell low K put | Width − debit | Debit | High K − debit |
| Long straddle | Big move | Buy ATM call + put | Unlimited | Premium | K ± premium |
| Long strangle | Big move, cheaper | Buy OTM call + put | Unlimited | Premium | K ± premium |

| Strategy | View | Legs | Max profit | Max loss | Breakeven |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Covered call | Neutral/mild bull | Stock + sell call | Premium + capped | Stock downside − premium | Cost − premium |
| Cash-secured put | Bullish/neutral | Sell put + cash | Premium | K − premium | K − premium |
| Protective put | Bullish + insurance | Stock + buy put | Unlimited | Capped | Cost + premium |
| Collar | Protect, low cost | Stock + buy put + sell call | Capped | Capped | Net cost |
| Bull put spread | Bullish | Sell high K put, buy low K put | Credit | Width − credit | High K − credit |
| Bear call spread | Bearish | Sell low K call, buy high K call | Credit | Width − credit | Low K + credit |
| Iron condor | Range | Sell OTM put/call, buy wings | Credit | Width − credit | Two BEs |
| Iron butterfly | Pin | Sell ATM call/put, buy wings | Credit | Width − credit | K ± credit |
| Short straddle | Low vol, pin | Sell ATM call + put | Premium | Large | K ± premium |
| Short strangle | Low vol, range | Sell OTM call + put | Premium | Large | K ± premium |

chunks.title: Module 06 — Derivatives & Options: Pricing, Greeks, Strategies > 7. Worked example — iron condor
chunks.text:
Module 06 — Derivatives & Options: Pricing, Greeks, Strategies > 7. Worked example — iron condor
7. Worked example — iron condor

Assume Nifty 25,000, lot 75 (verify), 30 days:

- Sell 24,500 PE at ₹80; buy 24,300 PE at ₹40 → credit ₹40.
- Sell 25,500 CE at ₹70; buy 25,700 CE at ₹35 → credit ₹35.
- Total credit ₹75 × 75 = ₹5,625.
- Max loss = (200 − 75) × 75 = ₹9,375.
- Breakevens: 24,425 and 25,575.
- Net Greeks: short gamma, positive theta, short vega, near delta-neutral.

**Failure modes:** large directional move, IV spike, expiry pin near a short strike,
liquidity widening the wings. Adjust by rolling the tested side or closing.

chunks.text:

9. Expiry-day dynamics

- **Gamma explosion:** ATM delta changes violently.
- **Theta acceleration:** premium decays fast.
- **Pinning:** price gravitates to high-OI strikes; can break.
- **Pin risk:** short ITM → assignment/delivery.
- **Margin:** intraday leverage may be cut.
- **SEBI 2024–25:** weekly expiry rationalisation, bigger contracts, intraday
  monitoring, ELM, reduced calendar-spread benefit on expiry day. Use current rules.

**Rule:** expiry day → smaller size, defined risk, no naked shorts.

chunks.title: Module 06 — Derivatives & Options: Pricing, Greeks, Strategies > 11. Indian F&O specifics
chunks.text:
Module 06 — Derivatives & Options: Pricing, Greeks, Strategies > 11. Indian F&O specifics
11. Indian F&O specifics

- Underlyings: Nifty, Bank Nifty, FinNifty, Midcap Select, Sensex, Bankex, stock F&O.
- Lot sizes revised periodically — check exchange contract specs.
- Expiry: weekly/monthly; day/shape changed in 2025 — verify.
- Index options: European, cash-settled.
- Stock options: American, physically settled.
- Margins: SPAN + exposure + ELM; peak margin; hedged benefit.
- STT: 0.1% sell premium; 0.02% futures sell.
- Ban list: OI >95% of MWPL → only reducing trades.
- Algo rules: broker approval, exchange registration, unique IDs.
- Assignment: short ITM options may be assigned.

chunks.title: Module 06 — Derivatives & Options: Pricing, Greeks, Strategies > 12. Options risk rules
chunks.text:
Module 06 — Derivatives & Options: Pricing, Greeks, Strategies > 12. Options risk rules
12. Options risk rules

1. Long premium: total loss <1% capital.
2. Short premium: size by max loss, not credit.
3. No naked short options for retail.
4. Defined-risk spreads for directional trades.
5. IV rank >70 → prefer credit; <30 → prefer debit.
6. Reduce/hedge before events; IV crush is brutal.
7. Trade liquid strikes with tight spreads.
8. Close/roll before expiry unless intentionally settling.
9. Keep 30–50% free margin.
10. Correlated index trades = one big bet.

chunks.title: Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 1. R and expectancy
chunks.text:
Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 1. R and expectancy
1. R and expectancy

```
R = entry − stop (long) or stop − entry (short)
R-multiple = (exit − entry)/R
Expectancy (R) = win%×avg win R − loss%×avg loss R
Expectancy (₹) = win%×avg win ₹ − loss%×avg loss ₹
Profit factor = gross profit/gross loss
Payoff ratio = avg win/avg loss
```

Example: 45% win, avg win 2R, avg loss 1R → expectancy = 0.9 − 0.55 = **+0.35R**.
100 trades → +35R before costs.

**Sample size:** 30 trades = rough; 100+ = confidence; regime shifts can invalidate.

---

chunks.title: Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 2. Position sizing > Fixed fractional (default)
chunks.text:
Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 2. Position sizing > Fixed fractional (default)
Fixed fractional (default)
```
Risk ₹ = capital × risk%
Quantity = Risk ₹/|entry − stop|
Position value = quantity × entry
```
Cap position value at 5–20% of capital and a % of average daily volume.

chunks.title: Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 2. Position sizing > ATR sizing
chunks.text:
Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 2. Position sizing > ATR sizing
ATR sizing
```
Stop = k×ATR (1.5–3)
Quantity = Risk ₹/(k×ATR)
```

chunks.title: Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 2. Position sizing > Volatility targeting
chunks.text:
Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 2. Position sizing > Volatility targeting
Volatility targeting
```
Exposure = (target vol/asset vol)×capital
```

chunks.title: Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 2. Position sizing > Kelly (theoretical)
chunks.text:
Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 2. Position sizing > Kelly (theoretical)
Kelly (theoretical)
```
f* = (b·p − q)/b
```
Use quarter/half Kelly at most; estimation error and fat tails make full Kelly dangerous.

chunks.title: Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 2. Position sizing > Options
chunks.text:
Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 2. Position sizing > Options
Options
Size by **max loss** (premium or width − credit), not by margin or credit received.

chunks.title: Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 3. Drawdown math
chunks.text:
Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 3. Drawdown math
3. Drawdown math

```
DD% = (peak − trough)/peak×100
Recovery gain = DD/(1−DD)
```

| DD | Recovery |
|---|---|
| 10% | 11.1% |
| 20% | 25% |
| 30% | 42.9% |
| 50% | 100% |
| 70% | 233% |
| 90% | 900% |

**Max DD** = worst peak-to-trough. **Calmar** = CAGR/Max DD.
**Risk of ruin** rises with risk per trade >2–3%, negative expectancy, leverage,
correlation, no stop.

**Rule:** DD >10% → halve risk; >15–20% → stop and rebuild.

---

chunks.title: Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 4. Portfolio risk
chunks.text:
Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 4. Portfolio risk
4. Portfolio risk

- Max single position: 5–10% trading; 15–20% long-term conviction.
- Max sector: 25–30%.
- Max factor exposure: 30–40%.
- Max correlated positions: 2–3.

```
Portfolio beta = Σ w_i×β_i
Hedge lots = (value×beta)/(futures price×lot size)
Correlation ρ = cov(A,B)/(σAσB)
```

Correlation >0.7 = one bet. Ten IT stocks is not diversification.

**Factors:** momentum, value, quality, low vol, size. Diversify across factors.

---

chunks.title: Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 5. VaR, CVaR and stress tests
chunks.text:
Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 5. VaR, CVaR and stress tests
5. VaR, CVaR and stress tests

**Parametric VaR (95%, 1-day):**
```
VaR = value × z × σ_daily; z95≈1.645, z99≈2.326
```
**Historical VaR:** 5th percentile of actual returns.
**CVaR:** average loss beyond VaR — better tail measure.

**Limitations:** normal assumptions, gaps, liquidity, fat tails.

**Stress scenarios:**
- 2008 −50% equity
- 2020 −30% in weeks
- Scam/liquidity shock
- Circuit breaker/halt
- Sector regulation
- Currency/rate spike
- IV doubling

---

chunks.title: Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 6. Monte Carlo
chunks.text:
Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 6. Monte Carlo
6. Monte Carlo

1. Estimate win rate, avg win R, avg loss R (with uncertainty).
2. Simulate 10,000 sequences of N trades.
3. Report median CAGR, 5th–95th percentile, max DD distribution, ruin probability.

**Sequence risk:** same average return, different drawdowns depending on order.

chunks.title: Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 7. Tail and gap risk
chunks.text:
Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 7. Tail and gap risk
7. Tail and gap risk

- **Gap:** overnight news/earnings/war → stop fills far away.
- **Circuit:** locked lower circuit → cannot exit.
- **Liquidity:** bid disappears.
- **Model:** correlations break.
- **Counterparty:** broker risk.

**Mitigations:** size for 2× stop gap, avoid leveraged binary events, use defined-risk
options, hedge tails, keep cash/free margin, diversify strategies.

---

chunks.title: Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 8. Risk policy template
chunks.text:
Module 07 — Risk Management: Survive First, Compound Later > 8. Risk policy template

```
Capital:
Max risk/trade: 0.5–1%
Max open risk: 3–6%
Max daily loss: 2%
Max weekly loss: 5%
Max monthly loss: 8–10%
Max trades/day: 3–5
Max correlated positions: 2–3
Max margin utilisation: 50–70%
Min free margin: 30%
Kill switch: 3 losses or daily limit → stop
Drawdown plan: 10% → half risk; 15–20% → stop
```

**Write it. Sign it. Review weekly.**

chunks.text:
Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty
Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty

**Level:** Advanced · **Time:** 8 hours · **Prerequisite:** Module 07

> Your strategy is a map. Psychology is the driver. A great map with a drunk driver
> still ends in a ditch.

chunks.title: Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > Learning outcomes
chunks.text:
Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > Learning outcomes
Learning outcomes

1. Identify the 15 biases that destroy trading accounts.
2. Recognise tilt early and apply a written protocol.
3. Separate process quality from outcome.
4. Build pre-market, intraday and post-market routines.
5. Complete a 21-day discipline challenge.

chunks.title: Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 1. The performance equation
chunks.text:
Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 1. The performance equation
1. The performance equation

```
Result = Edge × Risk × Consistency × Time − Costs − Emotional leakage
```

A 55% edge with 2% risk and no discipline loses to a 45% edge with 0.5% risk and
iron discipline. Your job: **reduce variance in execution**.

---

chunks.title: Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 2. Bias map
chunks.text:
Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 2. Bias map
2. Bias map

| Bias | Trading manifestation | Countermeasure |
|---|---|---|
| Loss aversion | Cut winners, hold losers | Pre-defined exits; judge R |
| Disposition effect | Sell winners, keep losers | Mechanical rules |
| Confirmation | Only bullish news | Write bear case first |
| Anchoring | "It was ₹500" | Value the future |
| Recency | Extrapolate last 3 trades | 100+ trade base rates |
| Overconfidence | Oversize after wins | Fixed risk |
| Hindsight | "I knew it" | Ex-ante journal |
| Sunk cost | Average down | "Would I enter now?" |
| Herding | Telegram tips | Independent checklist |
| Gambler's fallacy | "It's due" | No memory in markets |
| Revenge | Instant re-entry | Pause + daily limit |
| Narrative | Story over data | Numbers + invalidation |
| Authority | Blind experts | Verify track record |
| Endowment | Overvalue holdings | Pre-mortem |
| Mental accounting | "House money" | All capital is capital |
| Action bias | Boredom trading | No-trade is a position |

---

chunks.title: Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 3. The emotional cycle
chunks.text:
Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 3. The emotional cycle
3. The emotional cycle

```
Confidence → Overconfidence → Bigger size → Loss → Denial → Revenge →
Bigger loss → Fear → Paralysis → Missed opportunity → Frustration → ...
```

**Tilt warning signs:** checking P&L constantly, increasing size after a loss, widening
stops, "one more trade", blaming others, skipping the journal.

**Tilt protocol:**
1. Stop trading immediately.
2. Close platform, 30–60 min no screens.
3. Walk/breathe/hydrate.
4. Write what happened, what you felt, what rule broke.
5. No re-entry today.
6. Two tilt events/week → halve size for two weeks.

---

chunks.title: Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 4. Process vs outcome
chunks.text:
Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 4. Process vs outcome
4. Process vs outcome

| Process | Outcome | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Good | Good | Repeat |
| Good | Bad | Repeat (variance) |
| Bad | Good | Dangerous — don't reinforce |
| Bad | Bad | Fix immediately |

Grade every trade **A–F** on decision quality, independent of P&L:
- A: followed plan, right size, defined risk, journaled.
- B: minor deviation.
- C: skipped a check.
- D: no stop/revenge/FOMO.
- F: broke risk limits.

Track the correlation between grade and P&L over 50+ trades.

---

chunks.title: Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 5. Probabilistic thinking
chunks.text:
Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 5. Probabilistic thinking
5. Probabilistic thinking

- Every trade is one sample.
- Think expectancy, not "must win".
- You can be wrong 50% and still profitable.
- The market pays edge + discipline, not effort.

**Base-rate questions:**
1. Historical win rate for this setup?
2. Average R?
3. Which regime?
4. Cost drag?
5. Worst plausible outcome?

No answers = guessing → paper trade or tiny size.

---

chunks.title: Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 7. Journaling
chunks.text:
Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 7. Journaling
7. Journaling

Record decisions, not just outcomes. Minimum fields: date/time, instrument, setup,
regime, thesis, entry/stop/target/size/R, emotion, grade, mistake tag, MAE/MFE,
costs, lesson.

**Mistake taxonomy:** M01 no setup, M02 chase, M03 oversize, M04 no stop, M05 moved
stop, M06 early exit, M07 late exit, M08 revenge, M09 FOMO, M10 ignored event, M11
ignored regime, M12 wrong instrument, M13 overtrading, M14 averaged down, M15 execution,
M16 correlation.

chunks.title: Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 8. Confidence calibration
chunks.text:
Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 8. Confidence calibration
8. Confidence calibration

Keep a prediction log: "this trade hits 2R", "Nifty closes above X". Track how often
your 70% confidence is actually right. Most traders are overconfident on direction and
underconfident on risk.

chunks.title: Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 9. Loss-streak protocol
chunks.text:
Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 9. Loss-streak protocol
9. Loss-streak protocol

```
1 loss → normal
2 losses → size −25%, review
3 losses → stop for the day
5 losses → stop for the week, full review
DD >10% → halve risk
DD >15% → stop and rebuild
```

Never increase size to recover.

---

chunks.title: Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 10. Pre-mortem and if-then rules
chunks.text:
Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 10. Pre-mortem and if-then rules
10. Pre-mortem and if-then rules

**Pre-mortem:** imagine the trade lost. Write the 3 most likely reasons. Mitigate or
don't trade.

**Implementation intentions:**
- "If I want revenge, I close the platform and walk 10 min."
- "If price hits my stop, I exit without negotiation."
- "If I have 2 losses, I stop for the day."

---

chunks.title: Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 11. Lifestyle edge
chunks.text:
Module 08 — Trading Psychology: Discipline Under Uncertainty > 11. Lifestyle edge
11. Lifestyle edge

- Sleep <6h impairs risk judgment.
- 20–30 min exercise/day.
- Avoid heavy meals before market.
- Screen breaks every 60–90 min.
- Trading buddy/mentor for accountability.
- Trading capital ≠ rent/emergency fund.
- You are not your P&L.

chunks.text:

| Day | Task |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | Pre-market routine + journal every trade |
| 4–6 | No trades outside checklist; grade every decision |
| 7 | Weekly review + one fix |
| 8–10 | Fixed 1% risk; no size changes |
| 11–13 | No social media during market hours |
| 14 | Review tilt events |
| 15–17 | Paper trade one new setup; no real money |
| 18–20 | Follow kill switch strictly |
| 21 | Full audit: expectancy, mistakes, adherence |

Module 09 — Trading Systems & Quant: From Idea to Evidence
Module 09 — Trading Systems & Quant: From Idea to Evidence

**Level:** Advanced · **Time:** 14 hours · **Prerequisite:** Modules 03, 07

> Before building a system, choose the **style** it will trade — see
> [`course/14-trading-types/`](../14-trading-types/README.md). A system in the wrong
> style is still a losing system.

> A trading system is a set of **written rules** that can be tested, executed and
> reviewed. If it lives only in your head, it is a mood, not a system.

chunks.title: Module 09 — Trading Systems & Quant: From Idea to Evidence > 1. System anatomy
chunks.text:
Module 09 — Trading Systems & Quant: From Idea to Evidence > 1. System anatomy
1. System anatomy

```
Universe → Signal → Position sizing → Entry → Exit → Risk → Execution → Review
```

Every component must be **written and deterministic**:
- Universe: which stocks, liquidity filter, market cap.
- Signal: exact indicator/formula/threshold.
- Sizing: risk %, vol target, max positions.
- Entry: order type, timing, slippage assumption.
- Exit: stop, target, trailing, time stop, event exit.
- Risk: max open risk, correlation, drawdown limits.
- Execution: broker/API, reconciliation, kill switch.

---

chunks.title: Module 09 — Trading Systems & Quant: From Idea to Evidence > 2. Hypothesis and economic rationale
chunks.text:
Module 09 — Trading Systems & Quant: From Idea to Evidence > 2. Hypothesis and economic rationale
2. Hypothesis and economic rationale

A valid hypothesis:
1. What inefficiency? (behavioural, structural, risk premium, liquidity)
2. Why does it persist? (limits to arbitrage, capacity, regulation, fear)
3. Who is on the other side and why?
4. Which regime does it need?
5. Why would it stop working?

"RSI<30 buy" is a rule, not a hypothesis. Add the reason.

chunks.title: Module 09 — Trading Systems & Quant: From Idea to Evidence > 4. Seven deadly biases
chunks.text:

4. Seven deadly biases

| Bias | Fix |
|---|---|
| Look-ahead | Lag signals; point-in-time data |
| Survivorship | Include delisted |
| Selection | Pre-define universe/period |
| Overfitting | Few parameters; OOS |
| Data snooping | Pre-register; multiple-testing correction |
| Transaction costs | Model all costs |
| Liquidity | Next-open fills, volume caps, impact |

backfill, futures roll gaps.

chunks.title: Module 09 — Trading Systems & Quant: From Idea to Evidence > 5. Backtest engine
chunks.text:
Module 09 — Trading Systems & Quant: From Idea to Evidence > 5. Backtest engine
5. Backtest engine

Components: universe, signal, sizing, execution, costs, risk, accounting, reporting.

**Execution realism:**
- Signal at close → fill at next open.
- Slippage: 0.05–0.3% depending on liquidity.
- Costs: brokerage, STT, exchange, GST, stamp, DP.
- Lot sizes, tick sizes, circuit limits.
- Partial fills and volume caps.

**Vectorised vs event-driven:** vectorised for research, event-driven for validation.
