chunks.title: 🔬 Research Notes — What This Course Is Built On > 3. Options and Greeks
chunks.text:
🔬 Research Notes — What This Course Is Built On > 3. Options and Greeks
3. Options and Greeks

- Five primary Greeks: delta, gamma, theta, vega, rho.
- Delta: price sensitivity/hedge ratio; call 0 to 1, put −1 to 0.
- Gamma: change in delta; highest ATM near expiry.
- Theta: time decay; accelerates near expiry; ATM highest.
- Vega: IV sensitivity; highest ATM, longer-dated.
- Rho: rate sensitivity; small for short-dated.
- IV vs HV: high IV favours sellers, low IV favours buyers.
- IV crush around events.

Source: Investopedia — "Options Greeks" (updated Aug 2026).

Black-Scholes assumptions and put-call parity from standard derivatives texts (Hull).

---

chunks.title: 🔬 Research Notes — What This Course Is Built On > 4. Behavioural finance
chunks.text:
🔬 Research Notes — What This Course Is Built On > 4. Behavioural finance
4. Behavioural finance

- Investors are not always rational; biases are systematic.
- Key biases: loss aversion, overconfidence, herding, anchoring, confirmation,
  disposition effect, recency, hindsight, sunk cost, gambler's fallacy.
- Behavioural finance challenges EMH; anomalies can persist due to limits to arbitrage.
- Foundations: Mackay (1841), Le Bon, Selden (1912), Kahneman & Tversky, Thaler,
  Shiller.

Source: Wikipedia — Behavioural finance (accessed Nov 2026); Kahneman, *Thinking, Fast and Slow*.

---

chunks.title: 🔬 Research Notes — What This Course Is Built On > 5. Backtesting and overfitting
chunks.text:
🔬 Research Notes — What This Course Is Built On > 5. Backtesting and overfitting
5. Backtesting and overfitting

- Backtesting estimates how a strategy would have performed; limited by data quality,
  market impact, and overfitting.
- It is often possible to find a strategy that worked in the past but fails in the future.
- Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado, Zhu: "Pseudo-mathematics and financial charlatanism"
  — overfitting, deflated Sharpe ratio.
- Basel backtesting framework for VaR (green/orange/red zones) illustrates statistical
  validation.
- Robust methods: walk-forward, out-of-sample, Monte Carlo, parameter sensitivity,
  cost sensitivity, multiple-testing correction.

Source: Wikipedia — Backtesting (accessed Nov 2026); Bailey et al. (2014); López de Prado,
*Advances in Financial Machine Learning*.

---

chunks.title: 🔬 Research Notes — What This Course Is Built On > 6. Indian market rules (as of Nov 2026; check current circulars)
chunks.text:
🔬 Research Notes — What This Course Is Built On > 6. Indian market rules (as of Nov 2026; check current circulars)
6. Indian market rules (as of Nov 2026; check current circulars)

- T+1 settlement fully implemented (2023); T+0 optional expanding.
- UPI block mechanism for secondary market (2024).
- SEBI F&O measures 2024–25: larger contract sizes, weekly expiry rationalisation
  (one benchmark index per exchange), intraday position monitoring, ELM, reduced
  calendar-spread margin benefit on expiry day.
- Algo framework 2025: broker approval, exchange registration, unique algo ID.
- Capital gains post-July 2024: STCG 20%, LTCG 12.5% with ₹1.25 lakh exemption for
  listed equity; use current law.
- STT rates: delivery 0.1%, intraday 0.025% sell, futures 0.02% sell, options 0.1%
  sell premium (verify).
- Stock options physically settled; index options cash settled.
- F&O ban list at 95% of market-wide position limit.

**Data rule:** These rules change frequently. Every skill file points to the current
circular/source.

chunks.title: 🔬 Research Notes — What This Course Is Built On > 7. Course design principles
chunks.text:
🔬 Research Notes — What This Course Is Built On > 7. Course design principles
7. Course design principles

1. **India-first:** BSE/NSE history, SEBI, Indian costs/taxes, lot sizes, expiry.
2. **Risk-first:** risk management is 20% of the capstone grade.
3. **Evidence-based:** backtests with costs, OOS and Monte Carlo; results are probabilistic.
4. **Application:** every module has exercises and a deliverable.
5. **Psychology:** discipline is treated as a skill, not a personality trait.
6. **Compliance:** taxes and SEBI rules are part of the strategy, not an afterthought.
7. **Failure modes:** frameworks have limits; no single edge works in all regimes.

---

8. Limitations

- No live market data is embedded; users must fetch current prices.
- Tax/regulatory details are simplified and may change.
- Some frameworks (SMC/ICT, Elliott) are discretionary and have limited peer-reviewed
  evidence; the course explicitly labels them as lenses, not laws.
- Backtest examples are test cases, not signals.

chunks.text:
🔬 Research Notes — What This Course Is Built On > 9. 2024–2026 live-cycle research > 2024
2024
- **4 June 2024:** BJP won 240 seats; NDA reached a majority with allies. Sensex fell
  **4,389 points (−5.7%)** to 72,079; Nifty fell **5.9%** to 21,884. Markets recovered
  to new highs within weeks.
- **5 August 2024:** BoJ hike + weak US data triggered a global yen-carry unwind;
  Nikkei fell **12.4%** in a day (largest since 1987); India fell ~2.5–3%.
- **October 2024:** SEBI announced F&O measures — larger contract sizes, one weekly
  expiry per exchange, intraday position monitoring, higher margins. Effective from
  November 2024 onwards.

chunks.title: 🔬 Research Notes — What This Course Is Built On > 9. 2024–2026 live-cycle research > 2025
chunks.text:
🔬 Research Notes — What This Course Is Built On > 9. 2024–2026 live-cycle research > 2025
2025
- **2 April 2025:** US "Liberation Day" tariffs. S&P 500 fell about **19%** from its
  February 2025 peak to the April low; global market value losses ran into trillions.
  The S&P reclaimed its high by late June 2025 (~4 months from the February peak).
- **April–May 2025:** Pahalgam attack (22 April), Operation Sindoor (7 May), ceasefire
  (10 May). Indian equities saw a brief risk-off; defense stocks rallied.
- **27 August 2025:** US imposed 25% reciprocal tariff + 25% Russian-oil penalty =
  **50%** on many Indian goods. Exporters and the rupee came under pressure; domestic
  demand, GST cuts and RBI rate cuts cushioned the impact.
- **2 February 2026:** US–India trade deal reduced tariffs on Indian exports to **18%**;
  India agreed to stop buying Russian oil.

chunks.title: 🔬 Research Notes — What This Course Is Built On > 9. 2024–2026 live-cycle research > 2026
chunks.text:
🔬 Research Notes — What This Course Is Built On > 9. 2024–2026 live-cycle research > 2026
2026
- **28 February 2026:** US–Israel–Iran war began; Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was
  assassinated; Iran blocked the Strait of Hormuz. The IEA called it the largest
  supply disruption in the history of the global oil market. Brent peaked around
  **$118**.
- **30 March 2026:** S&P 500 bottomed at **6,316.91**.
- **8 April 2026:** initial ceasefire; relief rally. S&P rose **+17.3% to 7,411.98 by
  24 July 2026**. Brent fell to **$71.57 on 1 July**, then rose to **$100.69 on 23 July**
  and **$96.78 on 24 July**.
- **8 July 2026:** ceasefire collapsed; Iran attacked commercial vessels; oil and
  volatility returned. Houthi escalation followed in September–October.
- **May 2026 state elections:** BJP won West Bengal (Suvendu Adhikari became CM);
  TVK's Vijay became Tamil Nadu CM; UDF's V.D. Satheesan became Kerala CM; NDA/BJP
  retained Assam. **Not an election:** Karnataka's Congress government changed its
  Chief Minister to D.K. Shivakumar, replacing Siddaramaiah.
- **24 September 2026:** NSE listed on BSE; IPO raised ~**₹22,569 crore**, oversubscribed
  ~**5.71x**.
- **October 2026:** RBI signalled further rate hikes as oil-driven price pressures
  intensified. India's Q1 FY2026–27 GDP grew **7.8%**, above estimates.
- **November 2026:** Republican Party lost control of Congress in a landslide, widely
  attributed to the war's economic effects.

How to watch (anti-hype protocol)

1. **Mute tips.** Skip "buy this tomorrow" content.
2. **Take notes** with timestamps.
3. **Rebuild** any indicator/strategy yourself.
4. **Backtest** before believing.
5. **Check date** — market structure changes.
6. **Check incentives** — courses, brokering, affiliate links.
7. **One theme per week**, not random consumption.

chunks.title: calendar > purpose
chunks.text:
calendar > purpose
purpose: When NOT to trade. A calendar filter removes more bad trades than any indicator adds good ones.

chunks.title: calendar > principle
chunks.text:
calendar > principle
principle: Most signal damage comes from trading into known binary events with a technical stop that cannot protect against a gap.

chunks.title: calendar > hard_blocks > earnings_in_horizon
chunks.text:
calendar > hard_blocks > earnings_in_horizon
id: earnings_in_horizon
condition: Results date falls within horizon_days of the signal date
action: No signal.
why: A technical stop does not protect against a 15% earnings gap. The risk model assumes continuous prices; earnings break that assumption.

chunks.title: calendar > hard_blocks > fno_ban
chunks.text:
calendar > hard_blocks > fno_ban
id: fno_ban
condition: Underlying is in the F&O ban list
action: No derivative signal.
why: Fresh positions are prohibited. A signal that cannot be acted on is noise.

chunks.title: calendar > hard_blocks > circuit_recent
chunks.text:
calendar > hard_blocks > circuit_recent
id: circuit_recent
condition: Stock hit a circuit limit in the last 3 sessions
action: No signal.
why: Price discovery is broken. Indicators computed on circuit-locked prices are meaningless.

chunks.title: calendar > hard_blocks > data_stale
chunks.text:
calendar > hard_blocks > data_stale
id: data_stale
condition: Latest bar is older than 1 trading session
action: No signal.
why: A stale signal displayed as live is the most dangerous output this system can produce.

chunks.title: calendar > hard_blocks > corporate_action_pending
chunks.text:
calendar > hard_blocks > corporate_action_pending
id: corporate_action_pending
condition: Ex-date for split, bonus, or rights falls within horizon_days
action: No signal.
why: The price adjusts mechanically. Any target or stop computed on the pre-action basis is wrong.

chunks.title: calendar > soft_blocks > rbi_policy
chunks.text:
calendar > soft_blocks > rbi_policy
id: rbi_policy
condition: RBI monetary policy decision within 2 sessions
action: Halve position size.
why: Rate-sensitive sectors gap on the decision. Direction is not predictable from technicals.

chunks.title: calendar > soft_blocks > union_budget
chunks.text:
calendar > soft_blocks > union_budget
id: union_budget
condition: Union Budget within 5 sessions
action: Halve position size, avoid sector-specific bets.
why: Tax and duty changes reprice whole sectors overnight.

chunks.title: calendar > soft_blocks > monthly_expiry
chunks.text:
calendar > soft_blocks > monthly_expiry
id: monthly_expiry
condition: Monthly F&O expiry within 2 sessions
action: Avoid new derivative positions.
why: Gamma and roll flows distort intraday price action.

chunks.title: calendar > soft_blocks > results_season
chunks.text:
calendar > soft_blocks > results_season
id: results_season
condition: Peak results season (mid-Jan, mid-Apr, mid-Jul, mid-Oct)
action: Prefer setups with no results date in horizon; reduce size on the rest.
why: Idiosyncratic gap risk is elevated across the whole market.

chunks.title: calendar > soft_blocks > long_weekend
chunks.text:
calendar > soft_blocks > long_weekend
id: long_weekend
condition: Market closed for 3+ consecutive days
action: Avoid new swing entries in the last session before the break.
why: Overnight gap risk multiplies with the number of closed sessions.

chunks.title: calendar > never_trade_windows > first_15_minutes
chunks.text:
calendar > never_trade_windows > first_15_minutes
id: first_15_minutes
window: 09:15-09:30 IST
why: Opening auction residue and overnight order imbalance. Spreads are widest.

chunks.title: calendar > never_trade_windows > last_15_minutes
chunks.text:
calendar > never_trade_windows > last_15_minutes
id: last_15_minutes
window: 15:15-15:30 IST
why: Closing auction influence and position squaring. Intraday signals here are noise.

chunks.title: calendar > holiday_rule
chunks.text:
calendar > holiday_rule
holiday_rule: Use the exchange holiday calendar, not a weekday check. NSE has trading holidays that fall on weekdays, and muhurat sessions that fall on weekends.

chunks.title: calendar > data_source
chunks.text:
calendar > data_source
data_source: Corporate actions and results dates must be ingested from the exchange feed, not inferred. If the calendar is missing, treat the calendar filter as unknown and do not emit a signal.

chunks.title: costs > slippage
chunks.text:
costs > slippage
note: Costs above are taxes and fees. Slippage is separate and usually larger.
rule: Double the modelled slippage and re-run the backtest. If expectancy goes negative, the edge was never real.

chunks.title: costs > breakeven
chunks.text:
costs > breakeven
formula: total_cost_bps / 10000 must be exceeded by the average gross move
equity_intraday_example: 8.46 bps round trip means a 0.085% move just breaks even before slippage. Add 10 bps slippage and the bar is ~0.19%.
implication: High-frequency daily trading at ~30 round trips a month pays roughly 3% of capital per year in costs alone.

chunks.title: execution > purpose
chunks.text:
execution > purpose
purpose: Execution constraints that silently invalidate signals. These were absent from the course corpus (ban period: 0 mentions, adj_factor: 0 mentions).

chunks.title: execution > fno_ban_period
chunks.text:
execution > fno_ban_period
what: A stock enters the F&O ban list when open interest crosses 95% of the Market-Wide Position Limit (MWPL).
effect: No fresh derivative positions allowed. Existing positions may be squared off, not added to.
exit: The ban lifts when open interest falls back below the threshold (commonly cited around 80% of MWPL). Verify the current circular.
penalty: Trading fresh positions during the ban can attract a penalty of about 1% of the increased position value, with a minimum around Rs 5,000.
rule_for_signals: If the underlying is in the F&O ban list, do NOT emit a derivative signal. Cash-equity signals are unaffected.
data_source: NSE publishes fo_secban.csv daily. This must be ingested, not remembered.

chunks.title: execution > circuit_limits > stock_level
chunks.text:
execution > circuit_limits > stock_level
bands: 2%; 5%; 10%; 20%
rule: A stock stuck at the upper circuit cannot be bought; at the lower circuit it cannot be sold.
implication: A backtest that fills at the circuit price is wrong. The fill may not exist.
signal_rule: No new signal if the stock hit a circuit limit in the last 3 sessions.

chunks.title: execution > circuit_limits > index_level
chunks.text:
execution > circuit_limits > index_level
bands: 10%; 15%; 20%
rule: Exchange-wide circuit breakers halt trading for 15 minutes, 30 minutes, or the rest of the day depending on the level and time of hit.
implication: Intraday strategies must handle a market-wide halt as a hard risk event.

chunks.title: execution > corporate_actions > adj_factor
chunks.text:
execution > corporate_actions > adj_factor
what: A multiplier that restates historical prices onto today's share basis after splits, bonuses, and rights issues.
rule: Always compute returns on adjusted prices. Never stitch unadjusted prices across an action.
why_absent_from_course: The course corpus has zero mentions of adj_factor. This is the single largest source of fake data in Indian equity backtests.
verification: Check that the adjusted series has no single-day return beyond +/-20% for a largecap unless it is a real event.

chunks.title: execution > corporate_actions > dividends
chunks.text:
execution > corporate_actions > dividends
price_return_vs_total_return: Price return excludes dividends. Total return includes them.
rule: State which basis the backtest uses. Mixing them across strategies makes comparison meaningless.
note: NSEDATA4ME does not apply dividends. Price return only unless you add them.

chunks.title: execution > corporate_actions > ex_dates
chunks.text:
execution > corporate_actions > ex_dates
rule: Do not open a new position on the ex-date expecting the pre-action price. The price adjusts at open.

chunks.title: execution > settlement
chunks.text:
execution > settlement
equity: T+1 -- securities and funds settle one business day after trade.
implication: Capital is locked for one day in delivery trades. A daily rotation strategy cannot reuse the same capital every day.
fno: Mark-to-market daily; final settlement on expiry.

chunks.title: execution > order_mechanics
chunks.text:
execution > order_mechanics
tick_size: Rs 0.01 for most equity.
freeze_quantity: Large orders must be sliced. NSE publishes per-symbol freeze limits; index F&O freeze limits were revised with effect from October 2026. Verify current values.
spread_rule: Do not emit a signal when bid-ask spread exceeds 0.5% of price.
market_order_rule: Never model a market order fill at the last traded price. Model it at the far side of the spread plus slippage.

chunks.title: execution > regulatory > retail_algo_framework
chunks.text:
execution > regulatory > retail_algo_framework
effective: 1 April 2026
requires: Algo ID from the exchange; strategy registration through the broker; static IP whitelist; order rate limit around 10 orders per second
applies_to: Order-generating automation routed through a broker.
does_not_apply_to: A signal-only system that never places an order. This project is signal-only, so the framework does not bind it today -- but it binds the moment execution is added.

chunks.title: execution > regulatory
chunks.text:
execution > regulatory
research_analyst_note: Selling or distributing signals to others can bring you under Research Analyst regulation. Personal use and own capital is a different path. Get a lawyer before distributing anything.

chunks.title: failures > purpose
chunks.text:
failures > purpose
purpose: Failure modes per setup. This is the fuel for the mandatory Devil's Advocate field. A signal without a stated failure mode is an advertisement, not an analysis.

chunks.title: failures > rule
chunks.text:
failures > rule
rule: Prompt-level requirement: name at least one failure mode from this list for the setup being scored. The deterministic gate enforces presence, a 20-character minimum, and rejects literal generic cop-outs ('markets can go down'). It cannot verify list membership without a setup id, so treat membership as a review/eval check, not a gate guarantee.

chunks.title: failures > by_setup > trend_pullback > Trend exhaustion
chunks.text:
failures > by_setup > trend_pullback > Trend exhaustion
mode: Trend exhaustion
signs: ADX falling while price rises; 3+ distribution days in 10 sessions; volume rising on down days
consequence: Pullback becomes a reversal. The 50DMA break is the last exit.

chunks.title: failures > by_setup > trend_pullback > Late-stage entry
chunks.text:
failures > by_setup > trend_pullback > Late-stage entry
mode: Late-stage entry
signs: price more than 15% above 50DMA; 5th or later pullback in the same leg
consequence: Stop is far below, so position size shrinks and the trade is not worth the risk.

chunks.title: failures > by_setup > trend_pullback > False pullback low
chunks.text:
failures > by_setup > trend_pullback > False pullback low
mode: False pullback low
signs: pullback low formed on a gap down; support was never tested before
consequence: Stop sits at an untested level and gets swept.

chunks.title: failures > by_setup > range_breakout > False breakout (most common)
chunks.text:
failures > by_setup > range_breakout > False breakout (most common)
mode: False breakout (most common)
signs: breakout volume below 1.3x average; 4th+ touch of the range top; breakout on a gap, not on a close
consequence: Price re-enters the range within 3 sessions. This is the base rate, not the exception.

chunks.title: failures > by_setup > range_breakout > News-driven spike
chunks.text:
failures > by_setup > range_breakout > News-driven spike
mode: News-driven spike
signs: single-day volume above 4x average; no prior base building
consequence: Volume was a one-off event, not accumulation. The move mean-reverts.

chunks.title: failures > by_setup > range_breakout > Range top is also major resistance
chunks.text:
failures > by_setup > range_breakout > Range top is also major resistance
mode: Range top is also major resistance
signs: range top coincides with 200DMA or a prior all-time high
consequence: Two resistance layers stack; breakout needs disproportionate volume.

chunks.title: failures > by_setup > base_breakout > Wide and loose base
chunks.text:
failures > by_setup > base_breakout > Wide and loose base
mode: Wide and loose base
signs: base depth > 35%; ATR contraction inconsistent
consequence: Not a real contraction. Supply was never absorbed.

chunks.title: failures > by_setup > base_breakout > Breakout into overhead supply
chunks.text:
failures > by_setup > base_breakout > Breakout into overhead supply
mode: Breakout into overhead supply
signs: prior failed base 10-20% above; heavy volume-by-price node above
consequence: Buyers from the failed base sell into strength.

chunks.title: failures > by_setup > base_breakout > Earnings inside the horizon
chunks.text:
failures > by_setup > base_breakout > Earnings inside the horizon
mode: Earnings inside the horizon
signs: results date within horizon_days
consequence: Binary event. The technical stop does not protect against a gap.

chunks.title: failures > by_setup > rs_leader_pullback > Market regime flip
chunks.text:
failures > by_setup > rs_leader_pullback > Market regime flip
mode: Market regime flip
signs: Nifty breaks its 50DMA; breadth deteriorating while the leader holds
consequence: Leaders fall last and hardest in a market top.

chunks.title: failures > by_setup > rs_leader_pullback > Crowded leadership
chunks.text:
failures > by_setup > rs_leader_pullback > Crowded leadership
mode: Crowded leadership
signs: sector-wide extension; multiple leaders at 15%+ above 50DMA
consequence: The pullback is the exit liquidity for earlier buyers.

chunks.title: failures > by_setup > rs_leader_pullback > Relative strength is stale
chunks.text:
failures > by_setup > rs_leader_pullback > Relative strength is stale
mode: Relative strength is stale
signs: RS rank computed on unadjusted prices across a split; benchmark calendar misaligned
consequence: The rank is an artefact of bad data, not real outperformance.

chunks.title: failures > universal_failures > Survivorship bias
chunks.text:
failures > universal_failures > Survivorship bias
mode: Survivorship bias
signs: universe built from today's index members only
consequence: Backtest returns are inflated because delisted losers are missing.

chunks.title: failures > universal_failures > Look-ahead
chunks.text:
failures > universal_failures > Look-ahead
mode: Look-ahead
signs: signal uses the same close it trades on; features computed on the full series then split
consequence: The backtest is reading the future. Expectancy will collapse live.

chunks.title: failures > universal_failures > Corporate action contamination
chunks.text:
failures > universal_failures > Corporate action contamination
mode: Corporate action contamination
signs: adj_factor not applied; unadjusted series stitched across a split
consequence: A 1:10 split appears as a -90% crash and corrupts every indicator.

chunks.title: failures > universal_failures > Liquidity illusion
chunks.text:
failures > universal_failures > Liquidity illusion
mode: Liquidity illusion
signs: position size > 0.5% of 20-day average volume; smallcap with wide spreads
consequence: The backtest fill price does not exist at your size.

chunks.title: failures > universal_failures > Regime blind spot
chunks.text:
failures > universal_failures > Regime blind spot
mode: Regime blind spot
signs: one setup tested across all regimes without separation
consequence: A setup that works only in trend_up shows mediocre aggregate results and gets discarded incorrectly.

chunks.title: outcomes > purpose
chunks.text:
outcomes > purpose
purpose: How to label an outcome. Without this, 'win rate' is a number with no definition and learning cannot be measured.

chunks.title: outcomes > r_multiple
chunks.text:
outcomes > r_multiple
formula: R = (exit_price - entry_price) / (entry_price - stop_price) for longs; sign-flipped for shorts
meaning: Profit or loss expressed in units of initial risk. A 2R win means the trade made twice what was risked.
why: Percent returns are not comparable across trades with different stop distances. R is.

chunks.title: outcomes > horizon
chunks.text:
outcomes > horizon
rule: Every signal must declare horizon_days at emission time. It cannot be changed later.
exit_at_horizon: If neither stop nor target is hit by the horizon close, exit at that close and label time_exit.

chunks.title: outcomes > verdicts > win
chunks.text:
outcomes > verdicts > win
verdict: win
condition: r_multiple >= 1.0
note: A win is not 'price went up'. It is 'the trade made at least 1R'.

chunks.title: outcomes > verdicts > loss
chunks.text:
outcomes > verdicts > loss
verdict: loss
condition: r_multiple <= -1.0
note: A full stop-out. A partial stop that exits at -0.6R is a scratch, not a loss.

chunks.title: outcomes > verdicts > scratch
chunks.text:
outcomes > verdicts > scratch
verdict: scratch
condition: -1.0 < r_multiple < 1.0
note: Neither target nor full stop reached. Including these as wins inflates hit rate and hides a broken edge.

chunks.title: outcomes > excursions > MFE
chunks.text:
outcomes > excursions > MFE
name: Maximum Favourable Excursion
formula: max favourable price move during the hold, in R units
use: Tells you whether the target was too far. If MFE is consistently 1.2R but the target is 2.5R, the target is wrong.

chunks.title: outcomes > excursions > MAE
chunks.text:
outcomes > excursions > MAE
name: Maximum Adverse Excursion
formula: max adverse price move during the hold, in R units
use: Tells you whether the stop is too tight. If MAE regularly reaches -0.9R before the trade works, the stop will be hit by noise.

chunks.title: outcomes > ambiguity_rules > Both stop and target touched on the same daily bar
chunks.text:
outcomes > ambiguity_rules > Both stop and target touched on the same daily bar
case: Both stop and target touched on the same daily bar
rule: Assume the STOP was hit first. Daily OHLC cannot tell you the order.
why: Optimistic assumption here manufactures fake edge. Pessimistic is the only honest default.

chunks.title: outcomes > ambiguity_rules > Gap through the stop
chunks.text:
outcomes > ambiguity_rules > Gap through the stop
case: Gap through the stop
rule: Fill at the open, not at the stop price. R can be worse than -1.0.
why: Slippage on gaps is real. Ignoring it understates losses.

chunks.title: outcomes > ambiguity_rules > Gap through the target
chunks.text:
outcomes > ambiguity_rules > Gap through the target
case: Gap through the target
rule: Fill at the open, not at the target price. R can be better than planned.
why: Symmetric treatment. Do not take the good side only.

chunks.title: outcomes > ambiguity_rules > Corporate action during the hold
chunks.text:
outcomes > ambiguity_rules > Corporate action during the hold
case: Corporate action during the hold
rule: Adjust both entry and exit by adj_factor. Never compare unadjusted prices across an action.
why: A split looks like a -50% crash if unadjusted. That is fake data.

chunks.title: outcomes > ambiguity_rules > Stock hits circuit limit on exit day
chunks.text:
outcomes > ambiguity_rules > Stock hits circuit limit on exit day
case: Stock hits circuit limit on exit day
rule: Mark as unexit_at_limit and exclude from expectancy until a fill is possible.
why: A paper profit you cannot exit is not a profit.

chunks.title: outcomes > aggregation
chunks.text:
outcomes > aggregation
expectancy: mean(r_multiple) over closed trades
expectancy_floor: 0.0
min_sample: 100
report_alongside: win_rate; avg_win_R; avg_loss_R; max_drawdown_R; profit_factor
warning: A positive expectancy on fewer than 100 trades is not evidence. It is a small sample.

chunks.title: patterns > purpose
chunks.text:
patterns > purpose
purpose: Machine-readable candlestick pattern specifications. This file teaches the explanation layer what a detected pattern means; engine/patterns.py decides whether the pattern exists. The prose here is not executable.

chunks.title: patterns > global_rules
chunks.text:
patterns > global_rules
min_rr: 2.0
max_risk_per_trade_pct: 2.0
require_confirmation: True
trend_filter: Bullish reversal patterns need a prior decline or a range; bearish reversal patterns need a prior advance or a range. Continuation patterns need trend alignment.
volume_filter: The confirmation candle should trade at or above 1.5x the 20-day average volume.
location_filter: The pattern must sit at support, resistance, a moving average, or a range boundary. A pattern in the middle of nowhere is noise.
no_trade_if: pattern forms against a strong trend without confirmation; volume dries up on the confirmation candle; earnings or a corporate action falls inside the holding horizon; stock is in the F&O ban list; circuit limit was hit in the last 3 sessions; spread is wider than 0.5% of price

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Doji
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Doji
id: doji
name: Doji
category: single_candle
direction: neutral
bars: 1
structure: Open and close are almost equal; body is at most 10% of the high-low range.
psychology: Buyers and sellers finished the session at the same price. Neither side could hold control.
signal: Indecision. It is a pause, not a trade signal by itself.
entry: Wait for the next candle to break the doji high or low.
stop: Other side of the doji range after the break.
target1: 1R from the break.
target2: 2R from the break.
reliability: low
context_required: support_or_resistance; confirmation_candle
confirmation: next candle closes outside the doji range; volume expands on the break
false_signal: A doji in a quiet range produces many false breaks. A doji in the middle of a trend is usually continuation, not reversal.
notes: The doji is a location marker. Its value comes from where it appears, not from the shape alone.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Dragonfly Doji
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Dragonfly Doji
id: dragonfly_doji
name: Dragonfly Doji
category: single_candle
direction: bullish
bars: 1
structure: Open, high and close are almost equal; a long lower wick dominates the range.
psychology: Sellers pushed price sharply lower, but buyers absorbed the supply and closed the session at the high.
signal: Bullish rejection of lower prices, strongest after a decline or at support.
entry: Above the dragonfly high on the next candle.
stop: Below the dragonfly low.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing high.
reliability: medium
context_required: downtrend_or_range; support; volume_confirmation
confirmation: next candle closes above the dragonfly high; volume >= 1.3x 20D average
false_signal: Fails when the next candle opens below the dragonfly low; that turns the rejection into a continuation down.
notes: Shape is identical to a hammer with a very small body. Treat it as the same rejection idea.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Gravestone Doji
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Gravestone Doji
id: gravestone_doji
name: Gravestone Doji
category: single_candle
direction: bearish
bars: 1
structure: Open, low and close are almost equal; a long upper wick dominates the range.
psychology: Buyers pushed price sharply higher, but sellers took control and closed the session at the low.
signal: Bearish rejection of higher prices, strongest after an advance or at resistance.
entry: Below the gravestone low on the next candle.
stop: Above the gravestone high.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing low.
reliability: medium
context_required: uptrend_or_range; resistance; volume_confirmation
confirmation: next candle closes below the gravestone low; volume >= 1.3x 20D average
false_signal: Fails when the next candle opens above the gravestone high; that turns the rejection into a continuation up.
notes: Shape is identical to a shooting star with a very small body.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Hammer
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Hammer
id: hammer
name: Hammer
category: single_candle
direction: bullish
bars: 1
structure: Small body in the upper part of the range; lower wick at least 2x the body; little or no upper wick.
psychology: Sellers drove price down intraday, but buyers absorbed the supply and pushed the close back near the high.
signal: Potential bullish reversal after a decline.
entry: Above the hammer high on the next candle.
stop: Below the hammer low.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing high.
reliability: medium
context_required: downtrend_or_range; support; volume_confirmation
confirmation: next candle closes above the hammer high; volume >= 1.3x 20D average
false_signal: A hammer in a strong downtrend is often a pause before another leg down. No volume means no evidence.
notes: Same shape as hanging man; the preceding trend decides the label.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Hanging Man
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Hanging Man
id: hanging_man
name: Hanging Man
category: single_candle
direction: bearish
bars: 1
structure: Small body in the upper part of the range; lower wick at least 2x the body; little or no upper wick.
psychology: Sellers tested lower prices during an advance. Buyers recovered the close, but the intraday weakness is the first crack.
signal: Potential bearish reversal after an advance.
entry: Below the hanging man low on the next candle.
stop: Above the hanging man high.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing low.
reliability: low
context_required: uptrend; resistance; volume_confirmation
confirmation: next candle closes below the hanging man low; volume expands on the down candle
false_signal: Very common false reversal in strong uptrends. Needs a lower high or a broken short-term support to matter.
notes: Same shape as hammer; only the preceding advance makes it a hanging man.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Inverted Hammer
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Inverted Hammer
id: inverted_hammer
name: Inverted Hammer
category: single_candle
direction: bullish
bars: 1
structure: Small body in the lower part of the range; upper wick at least 2x the body; little or no lower wick.
psychology: Buyers tested higher prices. Sellers pushed the close back down, but the failed rally shows buyers are active.
signal: Potential bullish reversal after a decline, weaker than a hammer.
entry: Above the inverted hammer high on the next candle.
stop: Below the inverted hammer low.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing high.
reliability: low
context_required: downtrend_or_range; support; confirmation_candle
confirmation: next candle closes above the inverted hammer high; volume >= 1.3x 20D average
false_signal: Without a strong close above the high, it is just an intraday rally that failed.
notes: Same shape as shooting star; the preceding trend decides the label.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Shooting Star
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Shooting Star
id: shooting_star
name: Shooting Star
category: single_candle
direction: bearish
bars: 1
structure: Small body in the lower part of the range; upper wick at least 2x the body; little or no lower wick.
psychology: Buyers pushed price higher, but sellers rejected the move and closed the session near the low.
signal: Potential bearish reversal after an advance.
entry: Below the shooting star low on the next candle.
stop: Above the shooting star high.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing low.
reliability: medium
context_required: uptrend; resistance; volume_confirmation
confirmation: next candle closes below the shooting star low; volume expands on the down candle
false_signal: Fails in a strong uptrend when buyers immediately reclaim the high. Needs follow-through.
notes: Same shape as inverted hammer; only the preceding advance makes it a shooting star.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Bullish Marubozu
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Bullish Marubozu
id: bullish_marubozu
name: Bullish Marubozu
category: single_candle
direction: bullish
bars: 1
structure: Long green body with negligible upper and lower wicks; body is at least 90% of the range.
psychology: Buyers controlled the session from open to close. Sellers never mounted a meaningful counter-attack.
signal: Strong bullish conviction; continuation or breakout confirmation.
entry: Above the marubozu high, or on a shallow pullback that holds the body midpoint.
stop: Below the marubozu low.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the next resistance.
reliability: medium
context_required: trend_alignment; volume_confirmation
confirmation: volume >= 1.5x 20D average; close above nearby resistance
false_signal: A marubozu into resistance can be an exhaustion candle. Chasing the close is how traders buy the high.
notes: Best used as a confirmation candle, not as a standalone entry.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Bearish Marubozu
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Bearish Marubozu
id: bearish_marubozu
name: Bearish Marubozu
category: single_candle
direction: bearish
bars: 1
structure: Long red body with negligible upper and lower wicks; body is at least 90% of the range.
psychology: Sellers controlled the session from open to close. Buyers never mounted a meaningful counter-attack.
signal: Strong bearish conviction; continuation or breakdown confirmation.
entry: Below the marubozu low, or on a shallow bounce that fails at the body midpoint.
stop: Above the marubozu high.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the next support.
reliability: medium
context_required: trend_alignment; volume_confirmation
confirmation: volume >= 1.5x 20D average; close below nearby support
false_signal: A marubozu into support can be capitulation. Shorting the close is how traders sell the low.
notes: Best used as a confirmation candle, not as a standalone entry.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Spinning Top
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Spinning Top
id: spinning_top
name: Spinning Top
category: single_candle
direction: neutral
bars: 1
structure: Small body between 10% and 30% of the range, with upper and lower wicks each at least 20% of the range.
psychology: Both sides moved price, but neither could hold the close. Volatility without conviction.
signal: Indecision or pause. Wait for the range to break.
entry: Break of the spinning top high or low.
stop: Other side of the spinning top range.
target1: 1R from the break.
target2: 2R from the break.
reliability: low
context_required: location; confirmation_candle
confirmation: next candle closes outside the range; volume expands on the break
false_signal: Frequent in choppy ranges. The break often reverses within two sessions.
notes: A spinning top after a long trend can mark a pause; it is not a reversal by itself.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Bullish Pin Bar
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Bullish Pin Bar
id: bullish_pin_bar
name: Bullish Pin Bar
category: single_candle
direction: bullish
bars: 1
structure: Lower wick at least 66% of the range; body at most 34% of the range; upper wick small.
psychology: Price was rejected sharply from lower levels. The long wick is the footprint of absorbed selling.
signal: Bullish rejection, strongest at support or after a decline.
entry: Above the pin bar high on the next candle.
stop: Below the pin bar low.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing high.
reliability: medium
context_required: support; downtrend_or_range; volume_confirmation
confirmation: next candle closes above the pin bar high; volume >= 1.3x 20D average
false_signal: A pin bar in the middle of a range is noise. Location is the edge.
notes: A broader version of the hammer. The detector suppresses it when a hammer or doji already fired on the same bar.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Bullish Belt Hold
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Bullish Belt Hold
id: bullish_belt_hold
name: Bullish Belt Hold
category: single_candle
direction: bullish
bars: 1
structure: Green candle that opens at or near the low and closes near the high; body at least 70% of the range; almost no lower wick.
psychology: Buyers stepped in at the open and never let price trade below it. The session was one-sided.
signal: Bullish momentum, often the first candle of a reversal or breakout.
entry: Above the belt hold high on the next candle.
stop: Below the belt hold low.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing high.
reliability: medium
context_required: downtrend_or_range; support; volume_confirmation
confirmation: next candle holds above the belt hold open; volume >= 1.3x 20D average
false_signal: A belt hold into resistance can be a one-day squeeze. Needs follow-through.
notes: A weaker cousin of the bullish marubozu. The detector suppresses it when a marubozu already fired.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Bearish Belt Hold
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Bearish Belt Hold
id: bearish_belt_hold

category: single_candle

bars: 1

psychology: Sellers stepped in at the open and never let price trade above it. The session was one-sided.
signal: Bearish momentum, often the first candle of a reversal or breakdown.
entry: Below the belt hold low on the next candle.
stop: Above the belt hold high.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing low.
reliability: medium
context_required: uptrend_or_range; resistance; volume_confirmation

notes: A weaker cousin of the bearish marubozu. The detector suppresses it when a marubozu already fired.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Bullish Engulfing
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Bullish Engulfing
id: bullish_engulfing
name: Bullish Engulfing
category: two_candle
direction: bullish
bars: 2
structure: First candle bearish; second candle bullish; second body completely covers the first body; second body is larger.
psychology: Sellers had control, then buyers reversed the entire prior session and closed above its open. Control changed hands.
signal: Bullish reversal, strongest after a decline or at support.
entry: Above the engulfing candle high.
stop: Below the two-candle low.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing high.
reliability: medium
context_required: downtrend_or_range; support; volume_confirmation
confirmation: volume >= 1.5x 20D average on the engulfing candle; next candle holds above the engulfing open
false_signal: An engulfing candle in a strong downtrend is often a dead-cat bounce. Fails if the next candle closes below the two-candle low.
notes: One of the more reliable two-candle reversal patterns, but only with location and volume.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Bearish Engulfing
chunks.text:

notes: One of the more reliable two-candle reversal patterns, but only with location and volume.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Piercing Line
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Piercing Line
id: piercing_line
name: Piercing Line
category: two_candle
direction: bullish
bars: 2
structure: First candle bearish; second candle bullish; second opens below the first close and closes above the midpoint of the first body but below its open.
psychology: Sellers extended the decline, but buyers pushed the close deep into the prior body. The prior down move is losing force.
signal: Bullish reversal after a decline.
entry: Above the piercing candle high.
stop: Below the two-candle low.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing high.
reliability: medium
context_required: downtrend_or_range; support; volume_confirmation
confirmation: volume >= 1.3x 20D average on the second candle; next candle holds above the piercing close
false_signal: If the second close only reaches the midpoint, it is a weak bounce, not a piercing line.
notes: A less aggressive version of the bullish engulfing.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Dark Cloud Cover
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Dark Cloud Cover
id: dark_cloud_cover
name: Dark Cloud Cover
category: two_candle
direction: bearish
bars: 2
structure: First candle bullish; second candle bearish; second opens above the first close and closes below the midpoint of the first body but above its open.
psychology: Buyers extended the advance, but sellers pushed the close deep into the prior body. The prior up move is losing force.
signal: Bearish reversal after an advance.
entry: Below the dark cloud candle low.
stop: Above the two-candle high.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing low.
reliability: medium
context_required: uptrend_or_range; resistance; volume_confirmation
confirmation: volume >= 1.3x 20D average on the second candle; next candle holds below the dark cloud close
false_signal: If the second close only reaches the midpoint, it is a weak pullback, not a dark cloud cover.
notes: A less aggressive version of the bearish engulfing.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Bullish Harami
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Bullish Harami
id: bullish_harami
name: Bullish Harami
category: two_candle
direction: bullish
bars: 2
structure: First candle bearish and large; second candle bullish and small, with its body inside the first body.
psychology: The large down candle showed seller control. The small inside candle shows sellers could not extend the move; the market is pausing.
signal: Potential bullish reversal, weaker than an engulfing.
entry: Above the first candle high, or above the second candle high for a faster entry.
stop: Below the two-candle low.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing high.
reliability: low
context_required: downtrend_or_range; support; confirmation_candle
confirmation: next candle closes above the first candle open; volume expands on the confirmation
false_signal: A harami is a pause, not a reversal. Without a strong confirmation candle it often continues down.
notes: The inside body is the key. If the second body is not inside the first, it is not a harami.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Tweezer Bottom
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Tweezer Bottom
id: tweezer_bottom
name: Tweezer Bottom
category: two_candle
direction: bullish
bars: 2
structure: Two consecutive candles with nearly equal lows; the first bearish and the second bullish.
psychology: Sellers tested the same low twice and failed to break it. The double rejection builds a support level.
signal: Bullish reversal at support.
entry: Above the two-candle high.
stop: Below the equal lows.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing high.
reliability: low
context_required: support; downtrend_or_range; volume_confirmation
confirmation: next candle closes above the two-candle high; volume >= 1.3x 20D average
false_signal: Equal lows inside a downtrend are often a pause before a fresh breakdown. Needs a higher low to confirm.
notes: The two lows must be close relative to the recent range, not just numerically equal.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Tweezer Top
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Tweezer Top

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Inside Bar
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Inside Bar
id: inside_bar
name: Inside Bar
category: two_candle
direction: neutral
bars: 2
structure: The second candle's high is at or below the first high, and its low is at or above the first low.
psychology: Volatility contracted. The market is coiling inside the prior session's range.
signal: Compression before a breakout. Direction is unknown until the range breaks.
entry: Break of the mother bar high or low.
stop: Other side of the mother bar.
target1: 1R from the break.
target2: 2R from the break.
reliability: medium
context_required: trend_alignment; volume_confirmation
confirmation: close outside the mother bar range; volume expands on the break
false_signal: Inside bars are common; most breakouts fail in a range. Trade only with trend and volume.
notes: Also called a mother bar / inside bar setup. NR7 is a related volatility-contraction idea.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Outside Bar
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Outside Bar
id: outside_bar
name: Outside Bar
category: two_candle
direction: neutral
bars: 2
structure: The second candle's high is above the first high and its low is below the first low.
psychology: Volatility expanded in both directions. One side eventually won the session.
signal: Expansion. The close tells you which side won.
entry: Break of the outside bar high or low in the direction of the close.
stop: Other side of the outside bar.
target1: 1R from the break.
target2: 2R from the break.
reliability: medium
context_required: location; volume_confirmation
confirmation: close in the upper or lower third of the bar; volume >= 1.5x 20D average
false_signal: A outside bar with a close in the middle is a two-sided trap. No trade.
notes: The detector labels it neutral; the signal layer must use the close location to pick a side.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Bullish Kicker
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Bullish Kicker
id: bullish_kicker
name: Bullish Kicker
category: two_candle
direction: bullish
bars: 2
structure: First candle bearish; second candle bullish and opens above the first candle high; second body is strong.
psychology: Sentiment flipped overnight. Sellers were trapped and buyers gapped price above the prior session.
signal: Strong bullish reversal or continuation gap.
entry: Above the kicker candle high, or on the first shallow pullback that holds the gap.
stop: Below the kicker candle low, or below the gap.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing high.
reliability: high
context_required: downtrend_or_range; gap_context; volume_confirmation
confirmation: gap holds for the next 2 sessions; volume >= 1.5x 20D average
false_signal: Gaps fill often. A kicker without follow-through becomes a failed gap.
notes: One of the stronger two-candle signals because it requires a gap, not just a body reversal.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Morning Star
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Morning Star
id: morning_star
name: Morning Star
category: three_candle
direction: bullish
bars: 3
structure: First candle bearish and strong; second candle small and gapped below the first close; third candle bullish and closes above the midpoint of the first body.
psychology: Sellers dominated, then momentum stalled, then buyers reversed the move. The three sessions show a handover of control.
signal: Bullish reversal after a decline.
entry: Above the third candle high.
stop: Below the three-candle low.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing high.
reliability: high
context_required: downtrend_or_range; support; volume_confirmation
confirmation: third candle closes above the first body midpoint; volume >= 1.5x 20D average on the third candle
false_signal: If the third candle closes below the first midpoint, the reversal is weak. A morning star inside a strong downtrend often fails.
notes: The gap is not mandatory on all timeframes, but it strengthens the pattern.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Three White Soldiers
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Three White Soldiers
id: three_white_soldiers
name: Three White Soldiers
category: three_candle
direction: bullish
bars: 3
structure: Three consecutive bullish candles, each closing higher than the prior close, each opening at or above the prior open, with strong bodies.
psychology: Buyers showed up three sessions in a row and closed near the highs. Selling pressure is absent.
signal: Bullish continuation or reversal confirmation.
entry: Above the third candle high, or on a pullback that holds the first candle midpoint.
stop: Below the first candle low.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing high.
reliability: medium
context_required: trend_alignment; volume_confirmation
confirmation: volume stays above average across the three candles; no long upper wicks
false_signal: Three strong candles into resistance can be exhaustion. Chasing the third close is late.
notes: Best after a base or a pullback, not after a long extended run.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Three Black Crows
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Three Black Crows
id: three_black_crows
name: Three Black Crows
category: three_candle
direction: bearish
bars: 3
structure: Three consecutive bearish candles, each closing lower than the prior close, each opening at or below the prior open, with strong bodies.
psychology: Sellers showed up three sessions in a row and closed near the lows. Buying pressure is absent.
signal: Bearish continuation or reversal confirmation.
entry: Below the third candle low, or on a bounce that fails at the first candle midpoint.
stop: Above the first candle high.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing low.
reliability: medium
context_required: trend_alignment; volume_confirmation
confirmation: volume stays above average across the three candles; no long lower wicks
false_signal: Three strong down candles into support can be capitulation. Shorting the third close is late.
notes: Best after a distribution top or a failed rally, not after a long extended decline.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Three Inside Up
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Three Inside Up
id: three_inside_up
name: Three Inside Up
category: three_candle
direction: bullish
bars: 3
structure: First two candles form a bullish harami; the third candle is bullish and closes above the first candle open.
psychology: The harami showed sellers losing control; the third candle confirms buyers have taken over.
signal: Bullish reversal with confirmation.
entry: Above the third candle high.
stop: Below the three-candle low.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing high.
reliability: medium
context_required: downtrend_or_range; support; volume_confirmation
confirmation: third candle closes above the first candle open; volume expands on the third candle
false_signal: If the third candle closes back inside the first body, the confirmation failed.
notes: A harami plus a confirmation candle. Stronger than the harami alone.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Bullish Abandoned Baby
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Bullish Abandoned Baby
id: abandoned_baby_bullish
name: Bullish Abandoned Baby
category: three_candle
direction: bullish
bars: 3
structure: First candle bearish; second candle is a doji that gaps below the first candle low; third candle bullish and gaps above the doji, closing above the first body midpoint.
psychology: Sellers gapped price down, but the doji showed exhaustion. Buyers then gapped price back up, leaving the sellers stranded.
signal: Strong bullish reversal after a decline.
entry: Above the third candle high.
stop: Below the three-candle low.
target1: 1R.
target2: 2R, or the nearest swing high.
reliability: high
context_required: downtrend; support; volume_confirmation
confirmation: third candle closes above the first body midpoint; volume expands on the third candle
false_signal: Rare. If the gaps fill immediately, the pattern failed.
notes: A morning star with gaps on both sides of the doji. The gaps are the distinguishing feature.

chunks.title: patterns > patterns > Tri-Star
chunks.text:
patterns > patterns > Tri-Star
id: tri_star
name: Tri-Star
category: three_candle
direction: neutral
bars: 3
structure: Three consecutive dojis.
psychology: The market has stalled for three sessions. Neither side can hold a close.
signal: Strong indecision. Wait for the range to break.
entry: Break of the three-candle high or low.
stop: Other side of the three-candle range.
target1: 1R from the break.
target2: 2R from the break.
reliability: low
context_required: location; confirmation_candle
confirmation: next candle closes outside the three-candle range; volume expands on the break
false_signal: A tri-star in a quiet range is noise. The break often fails.
notes: Rare. Treat it as a compression marker, not a directional signal.

chunks.title: regimes > purpose
chunks.text:
regimes > purpose
purpose: Operational regime definitions. 'Trend' must be a measurable state, not an opinion. Every threshold here is computed from data, never assigned by the model.

chunks.title: regimes > computed_by
chunks.text:
regimes > computed_by
computed_by: engine/features (deterministic code). The LLM may read the label; it may not invent it.

chunks.text:
regimes > regimes > trend_up > criteria
all_of: close > 200DMA; 50DMA > 200DMA; ADX(14) >= 20; slope of 50DMA over 20 sessions > 0

regimes > regimes > trend_up
id: trend_up

tradeable_setups: trend_pullback; base_breakout; rs_leader_pullback

chunks.title: setups > purpose
chunks.text:
setups > purpose
purpose: Machine-readable setup specifications. Prose is not executable; these are.

chunks.title: setups > global_rules
chunks.text:
setups > global_rules
min_rr: 2.0
min_rr_is_absolute: True
min_rr_note: This floor has no per-setup exceptions. A mean-reversion setup needs a 1.5R target to be mean reversion at all, so it cannot clear this bar and is deliberately excluded. Weakening the floor for one setup weakens it for all of them.
max_risk_per_trade_pct: 2.0
require_regime_match: True
require_confirmation: True
no_trade_if: stock in F&O ban list; earnings within horizon_days; circuit limit hit in last 3 sessions; data older than 1 trading session; spread > 0.5% of price

chunks.title: setups > setups > Trend Pullback Continuation
chunks.text:
setups > setups > Trend Pullback Continuation
id: trend_pullback
name: Trend Pullback Continuation
style: swing
timeframe: daily
horizon_days: 10
regime_required: trend_up
entry: Close above prior day high after a 3-8 session pullback that holds above the 20DMA and does not close below the 50DMA.
stop: Below the pullback low, or 1.5 x ATR(14) below entry, whichever is closer.
target: Prior swing high; if already exceeded, 2.5 x initial risk.
invalidation: Daily close below the 50DMA, or the pullback low is broken before entry.
confirmation: pullback volume below 20D average; breakout volume above 1.3 x 20D average; RSI(14) between 40 and 65 at the pullback low
min_rr: 2.0
notes: This is the highest-expectancy setup for daily data. It fails in choppy ranges, which is why regime_required is enforced.

chunks.title: setups > setups > Range Breakout with Volume
chunks.text:
setups > setups > Range Breakout with Volume
id: range_breakout
name: Range Breakout with Volume
style: swing
timeframe: daily
horizon_days: 10
regime_required: range; transition
entry: Daily close above the top of a range that has held for at least 15 sessions.
stop: Below the range midpoint, or 2 x ATR(14) below entry.
target: Range height projected from the breakout point.
invalidation: Close back inside the range within 3 sessions (failed breakout).
confirmation: volume >= 1.5 x 20D average on the breakout day; range width between 4% and 15% of price; no more than 3 touches of the range top before the break
min_rr: 2.0
notes: Most breakouts fail. The 3-session re-entry rule is the filter; without it this setup has negative expectancy.

chunks.title: setups > setups > Volatility Contraction Base Breakout
chunks.text:
setups > setups > Volatility Contraction Base Breakout
id: base_breakout
name: Volatility Contraction Base Breakout
style: positional
timeframe: daily
horizon_days: 20
regime_required: trend_up; transition
entry: Close above the pivot of a base where ATR has contracted for at least 3 consecutive weeks.
stop: Below the base low, or 7% below entry, whichever is closer.
target: 2.5 x initial risk, trailed after +1R.
invalidation: Base low broken, or ATR expands without a price breakout.
confirmation: ATR(14) at a 3-month low before the breakout; volume dry-up in the final third of the base; breakout volume above 1.5 x 20D average
min_rr: 2.5
notes: Needs a longer horizon than trend_pullback. Do not apply this on a 5-day horizon.

chunks.title: setups > setups > Relative Strength Leader Pullback
chunks.text:
setups > setups > Relative Strength Leader Pullback
id: rs_leader_pullback
name: Relative Strength Leader Pullback
style: positional
timeframe: daily
horizon_days: 20
regime_required: trend_up
entry: Stock in the top decile of 3-month relative strength vs Nifty, pulling back to the 20DMA and closing above it.
stop: Below the 50DMA, or 2 x ATR(14) below entry.
target: 2.5 x initial risk, trailed.
invalidation: Relative strength rank drops below the 50th percentile, or the 50DMA breaks.
confirmation: 3-month RS rank >= 90th percentile; pullback volume below average; market regime is trend_up, not range
min_rr: 2.5
notes: Requires a benchmark series (Nifty) aligned on the same calendar. Without it, do not emit this setup.
